      "content": "1|*A Tier 1 Free League of Stickyickistan adventure for four to five 3rd-level characters*
2|
3|# Introduction
4|
5|**Curse of Slaad** is a short monster-hunt adventure set in [[Stickyickistan]] and designed for a three- to four-hour session. The characters investigate disappearances and corrupted crops in [[North Booftown]], the city-state’s agricultural heartland. The infestation begins near [[Astallon Acres]], along the wetlands bordering [[Zooka Mire]], and threatens the region’s livestock, farm workers, and [[Arcannabis]] fields.
6|
7|The adventure is intended to feel like swampy horror-comedy: gross, weird, dangerous, and slightly ridiculous. Emphasize wet croaks, twitching vegetation, sour compost smells, and the unsettling sight of tiny frog-things working together.
8|
9|## Adventure Background
10|
11|The infestation began when contaminated [[Arcannabis]] fertilizer was dumped near an abandoned agricultural greenhouse on the edge of [[Astallon Acres]]. A planar spore within the waste infected the greenhouse’s irrigation system, mutating the plants and creating the first slaad tadpoles. The residue at the heart of the nest can later reveal whether the contamination was accidental or deliberate.
12|
13|At the center of the infestation is a **Red Slaad**, a violent extraplanar predator that protects its spawn and feeds victims into the nest. Unless the infestation is stopped, the slaad will spread through the farms of [[North Booftown]], into [[Zooka Mire]], and eventually toward Stickyickistan’s food and Arcannabis production.
14|
15|## Adventure Hook
16|
17|The adventure begins when the characters are hired by [[Ezra Astallon]], the wealthy owner of [[Astallon Acres]]. His workers have reported missing livestock, corrupted crops, and two missing farmhands near an abandoned agricultural greenhouse. Ezra wants the problem solved before it damages his harvest or attracts the attention of the [[Nevercough Tribunal]].
18|
19|After accepting the job, the characters travel into [[North Booftown]] and begin Part 1 when they arrive at the first damaged farmstead.
20|
21|### Opening Scene
22|
23|Read or paraphrase:
24|
25|> The farmstead lies at the edge of [[Astallon Acres]], where cultivated fields give way to wet ground and tangled reeds. Rows of Arcannabis plants lean toward the road, their leaves swollen and darkened with a greasy green film.
26|>
27|> The livestock pens stand open and empty. A broken fence disappears beneath a mat of vines, and something wet has dragged a furrow through the mud toward the distant wetlands.
28|>
29|> [[Ezra Astallon]] waits beside the farmhouse, dressed too well for the mud and speaking in a low, impatient voice.
30|>
31|> “The animals vanished first. Then two workers went looking for them. The crops began changing yesterday. If this reaches the rest of North Booftown, we could lose half the harvest.”
32|>
33|> From beyond the fields, something croaks.
34|>
35|> A smaller voice answers from somewhere beneath the reeds.
36|
37|Ezra provides the characters with directions to the abandoned greenhouse and promises payment for stopping the infestation. The characters then begin Part 1 by interviewing farm workers, examining the damaged crops, or following the first slime trail.
38|
39|### Rumors
40|
41|The characters may hear one or more of the following rumors before reaching the greenhouse:
42|
43|| d6 | Rumor |
44||---:|---|
45|| 1 | “The plants move after sunset. I saw vines dragging a goat uphill.” |
46|| 2 | “There’s croaking in the irrigation channels, but no frogs in the fields anymore.” |
47|| 3 | “One body came back half-melted, like something had tried to compost him.” |
48|| 4 | “Tiny slaad tadpoles have been seen carrying scraps toward the old greenhouse.” |
49|| 5 | “Fire scares them. Or maybe it just makes them angry.” |
50|| 6 | “The greenhouse was sealed after the last crop failed. Nobody remembers who locked it.”
51|
52|---
53|
54|# Part 1: Investigation
55|
56|*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*
57|
58|Part 1 begins when the characters arrive at the damaged farmstead in [[Astallon Acres]]. They investigate the missing livestock and workers, inspect the corrupted Arcannabis fields, and follow signs toward the abandoned greenhouse near [[Zooka Mire]]. They do not need to discover every clue. Two or three successful investigation scenes are enough to point them toward the Outer Nest.
59|
60|---
61|
62|# Part 1: Investigation
63|
64|*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*
65|
66|Part 1 begins when the characters arrive at the damaged farmstead in [[Astallon Acres]]. They investigate the missing livestock and workers, inspect the corrupted Arcannabis fields, and follow signs toward the abandoned greenhouse near [[Zooka Mire]]. They do not need to discover every clue. Two or three successful investigation scenes are enough to point them toward the Outer Nest.
67|
68|Read or paraphrase:
69|
70|> The air grows wet and green as you approach the infected ground. Leaves shine with a greasy film, and the soil gives slightly beneath each step, as though the earth itself has gone soft.
71|>
72|> Somewhere ahead, something croaks.
73|>
74|> Then something smaller croaks back.
75|
76|## Investigation Scenes
77|
78|Use two or three of the following scenes. Each scene should provide a clue even if the characters fail a check. A failed check may cost time, attract attention, or create a later complication.
79|
80|### Frightened Locals
81|
82|Witnesses describe missing livestock, moving plants, strange croaking, and small creatures dragging food into the brush.
83|
84|**Useful Checks:**
85|
86|- **DC 11 Charisma (Persuasion):** Calm witnesses and get a clear description.
87|- **DC 11 Wisdom (Insight):** Notice that witnesses are more frightened by the croaking than by the plants.
88|- **DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation):** Piece together that the disappearances are spreading outward from one central site.
89|
90|**Clue:** The creatures are collecting food rather than merely attacking at random.
91|
92|### Damaged Crops or Bodies
93|
94|The party finds ruined crops, slime-burned fences, half-eaten livestock, or a partially dissolved corpse.
95|
96|**Useful Checks:**
97|
98|- **DC 11 Intelligence (Nature):** Identify that the plants are growing too quickly and feeding on organic remains.
99|- **DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine):** Determine that acid or digestive slime caused the injuries.
100|- **DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana):** Sense planar or chaotic magic in the residue.
101|
102|**Clue:** The infestation is both botanical and extraplanar, and it is converting organic matter into growth.
103|
104|### Slime Trail
105|
106|A slick trail leads toward the nest. Tiny webbed prints and dragged scraps of food mark the path.
107|
108|**Useful Checks:**
109|
110|- **DC 11 Wisdom (Survival):** Follow the trail.
111|- **DC 13 Wisdom (Perception):** Spot hidden tadpoles watching from the brush.
112|- **DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth):** Approach without alerting the outer nest.
113|
114|**Clue:** The trail leads toward an overgrown structure, drainage tunnel, or root-choked hollow where the creatures are nesting.
115|
116|## Clues
117|
118|Reward good investigation with one or more of the following clues:
119|
120|- The smaller creatures are spawn and will defend egg clusters.
121|- A larger creature protects the tadpoles at all costs.
122|- Fire frightens or disrupts the plant growth.
123|- The lair has hidden entrances through roots, drains, or burrows.
124|- The nest is feeding on victims to grow more spawn.
125|- The infestation is spreading outward from a central chamber.
126|
127|Once the characters have enough information, proceed to Part 2.
128|
129|---
130|
131|# Part 2: The Outer Nest
132|
133|*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*
134|
135|The characters enter the infected area. This section establishes the danger and drains a few resources without overshadowing the final encounter.
136|
137|Read or paraphrase:
138|
139|> The path disappears beneath thick vines and glossy leaves. Bulging pods hang from branches like wet fruit. Greenish slime trembles in shallow puddles whenever something croaks nearby.
140|>
141|> Small shapes move beneath the leaves.
142|>
143|> One of them stops.
144|>
145|> Then all of them start croaking at once.
146|
147|## Encounter: Salad Tadpoles
148|
149|Use **4–8 Salad Tadpoles**, depending on party size and remaining resources. The tadpoles harass the party, retreat through small gaps, and try to draw intruders toward hazards rather than fight to the death.
150|
151|If custom statistics are unavailable, use low-CR frog, twig blight, or crawling claw-style creatures and describe their attacks as acidic, poisonous, or vine-based.
152|
153|The tadpoles should reveal the nest’s behavior during this encounter. They defend routes to the inner chambers, but they prioritize sounding alarms and protecting egg clusters over killing intruders.
154|
155|## Outer Nest Hazards
156|
157|Choose or roll one hazard. A hazard can occur during the tadpole encounter or immediately afterward.
158|
159|| d4 | Hazard |
160||---:|---|
161|| 1 | **Acidic Pollen.** A disturbed pod bursts. Creatures within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take acid damage and cough loudly, alerting the nest. |
162|| 2 | **Grasping Vines.** Vines turn the area into difficult terrain. A creature that dashes must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. |
163|| 3 | **Slime Sink.** A patch of ground collapses into digestive muck. A creature that enters it must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or become restrained until freed. |
164|| 4 | **Croaking Alarm.** Tadpoles begin a rhythmic chorus. If they are not stopped within 2 rounds, the Red Salad is alert during the final encounter and cannot be surprised. |
165|
166|---
167|
168|# Part 3: The Heart of the Nest
169|
170|*Estimated Duration: 60–75 minutes*
171|
172|The heart of the nest is a wet chamber, greenhouse, root cellar, sewer dome, or druidic hollow filled with egg sacs and nutrient slime. Choose details that fit the location established during the investigation.
173|
174|Read or paraphrase:
175|
176|> The nest opens before you in a pulse of wet heat and sour green stink. Egg sacs cling to roots and cracked stone. Slime pools bubble between heaps of bones, tools, boots, and half-digested packs.
177|>
178|> At the center of it all squats something red, swollen, and alive with twitching leaves. Its throat inflates.
179|>
180|> The whole chamber croaks back.
181|
182|## Boss Encounter
183|
184|Enemies:
185|
186|- **1 Red Salad**
187|- **Several Salad Tadpoles**
188|
189|If custom statistics are unavailable, use a suitable plant, frog, or slaad-like stat block for the Red Salad and reskin its attacks with acid, vines, and tongue strikes.
190|
191|The final encounter has three simultaneous objectives: defeat the Red Salad, prevent more tadpoles from hatching, and stop the creature from escaping into the surrounding area.
192|
193|## Egg Clusters
194|
195|Place **3 egg clusters** around the battlefield.
196|
197|- Each egg cluster has AC 10 and 10 hit points.
198|- Fire damage destroys an egg cluster immediately.
199|- At the end of every other round, one intact egg cluster hatches **1 Salad Tadpole**.
200|- Destroying all egg clusters stops new tadpoles from appearing.
201|
202|## Red Salad Tactics
203|
204|The Red Salad is protective and territorial.
205|
206|- It prioritizes characters attacking egg clusters.
207|- It uses tadpoles and terrain to slow enemies.
208|- It retreats toward underground tunnels if reduced to low hit points.
209|- Once per fight, it may consume a nearby tadpole or egg cluster to regain hit points.
210|- If escape is possible, it tries to reach a secondary chamber rather than fight in an exposed area.
211|
212|## Battlefield Features
213|
214|| Feature | Effect |
215||---|---|
216|| Acid Pools | A creature that enters a pool or starts its turn there takes acid damage. |
217|| Hanging Vines | Provide half cover and can be cut or burned. |
218|| Nutrient Slime | Plant creatures that start their turn in the slime regain a small amount of hit points. |
219|| Rotten Walkways | A creature that takes heavy damage while standing on one may need to save or fall. |
220|| Egg Sacs | Hatch tadpoles if ignored. |
221|
222|## Objectives Beyond Killing Everything
223|
224|The characters may also:
225|
226|- Destroy the egg clusters.
227|- Rescue an NPC wrapped in roots.
228|- Prevent the Red Salad from escaping into underground tunnels.
229|- Recover the strange seed or planar spore at the heart of the nest.
230|- Secure samples without allowing the infestation to spread.
231|
232|---
233|
234|# Part 4: Conclusion
235|
236|*Estimated Duration: 30 minutes*
237|
238|When the Red Salad is defeated and the egg clusters are destroyed, the infestation begins to collapse. Vines loosen, slime pools dry into crust, and the constant croaking finally stops.
239|
240|If the characters do not destroy the egg clusters, the infestation survives even if the Red Salad dies. The surviving spawn may retreat into drains, roots, or nearby farmland.
241|
242|## Possible Rewards
243|
244|- Payment from the employer.
245|- Harvested monster parts using [[Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting]].
246|- A strange magical seed or planar spore.
247|- Acid glands, sticky slime, or volatile spores.
248|- A clue pointing toward another infestation.
249|- Gratitude from farmers, apothecaries, or local residents.
250|
251|## Lingering Consequences
252|
253|Choose one or more:
254|
255|- A surviving tadpole escapes into the drainage system.
256|- The strange seed remains valuable but faintly alive.
257|- Infected soil can be purified, sold, studied, or misused.
258|- A faction wants the remains for research.
259|- Someone insists the infestation was not an accident.
260|- Destroying the nest releases a burst of planar energy that mutates nearby plants.
261|
262|---
263|
264|# Difficulty
265|
266|For **four to five 3rd-level characters**, use the following progression:
267|
268|| Encounter | Difficulty |
269||---|---|
270|| Investigation obstacle | Easy |
271|| Outer Nest tadpoles and hazard | Medium |
272|| Optional hazard or ambush | Easy–Medium |
273|| Red Salad and tadpoles | Hard |
274|
275|The final fight is usually sufficient if the party has already spent some spells, hit points, or class resources in the Outer Nest.
276|
277|---
278|
279|# DM Notes
280|
281|## Tone
282|
283|Keep the adventure swampy, gross, and strange rather than relentlessly grim. The danger should feel real, but the creature’s behavior can remain bizarre and darkly funny. Emphasize coordinated tadpoles, absurdly wet vegetation, sour smells, and the unsettling transformation of victims into fertilizer.
284|
285|## Scaling
286|
287|- For a weaker party, use fewer tadpoles, reduce the number of egg clusters to two, and remove one battlefield hazard.
288|- For a stronger party, add tadpoles, allow two egg clusters to hatch at once, or give the Red Salad an additional use of its strongest ability.
289|- For a shorter session, skip the Outer Nest combat and use one investigation hazard before the boss.
290|- For a longer session, add a trapped NPC, rival hunters, or a faction trying to steal samples.
291|
292|## Harvest Ideas
293|
294|- Red Salad tongue
295|- Acidic digestive slime
296|- Slaad-touched seed
297|- Tadpole glands
298|- Egg cluster membrane
299|- Planar compost

      "content": "1|*A Tier 1 Free League of Stickyickistan adventure for four to five 3rd-level characters*
2|
3|# Introduction
4|
5|**Curse of Slaad** is a short monster-hunt adventure set in [[Stickyickistan]] and designed for a three- to four-hour session. The characters investigate disappearances and corrupted crops in [[North Booftown]], the city-state’s agricultural heartland. The infestation begins near [[Astallon Acres]], along the wetlands bordering [[Zooka Mire]], and threatens the region’s livestock, farm workers, and [[Arcannabis]] fields.
6|
7|The adventure is intended to feel like swampy horror-comedy: gross, weird, dangerous, and slightly ridiculous. Emphasize wet croaks, twitching vegetation, sour compost smells, and the unsettling sight of tiny frog-things working together.
8|
9|## Adventure Background
10|
11|The infestation began when contaminated [[Arcannabis]] fertilizer was dumped near an abandoned agricultural greenhouse on the edge of [[Astallon Acres]]. A planar spore within the waste infected the greenhouse’s irrigation system, mutating the plants and creating the first slaad tadpoles. The residue at the heart of the nest can later reveal whether the contamination was accidental or deliberate.
12|
13|At the center of the infestation is a **Red Slaad**, a violent extraplanar predator that protects its spawn and feeds victims into the nest. Unless the infestation is stopped, the slaad will spread through the farms of [[North Booftown]], into [[Zooka Mire]], and eventually toward Stickyickistan’s food and Arcannabis production.
14|
15|## Adventure Hook
16|
17|The adventure begins when the characters are hired by [[Ezra Astallon]], the wealthy owner of [[Astallon Acres]]. His workers have reported missing livestock, corrupted crops, and two missing farmhands near an abandoned agricultural greenhouse. Ezra wants the problem solved before it damages his harvest or attracts the attention of the [[Nevercough Tribunal]].
18|
19|After accepting the job, the characters travel into [[North Booftown]] and begin Part 1 when they arrive at the first damaged farmstead.
20|
21|### Opening Scene
22|
23|Read or paraphrase:
24|
25|> The farmstead lies at the edge of [[Astallon Acres]], where cultivated fields give way to wet ground and tangled reeds. Rows of Arcannabis plants lean toward the road, their leaves swollen and darkened with a greasy green film.
26|>
27|> The livestock pens stand open and empty. A broken fence disappears beneath a mat of vines, and something wet has dragged a furrow through the mud toward the distant wetlands.
28|>
29|> [[Ezra Astallon]] waits beside the farmhouse, dressed too well for the mud and speaking in a low, impatient voice.
30|>
31|> “The animals vanished first. Then two workers went looking for them. The crops began changing yesterday. If this reaches the rest of North Booftown, we could lose half the harvest.”
32|>
33|> From beyond the fields, something croaks.
34|>
35|> A smaller voice answers from somewhere beneath the reeds.
36|
37|Ezra provides the characters with directions to the abandoned greenhouse and promises payment for stopping the infestation. The characters then begin Part 1 by interviewing farm workers, examining the damaged crops, or following the first slime trail.
38|
39|### Rumors
40|
41|The characters may hear one or more of the following rumors before reaching the greenhouse:
42|
43|| d6 | Rumor |
44||---:|---|
45|| 1 | “The plants move after sunset. I saw vines dragging a goat uphill.” |
46|| 2 | “There’s croaking in the irrigation channels, but no frogs in the fields anymore.” |
47|| 3 | “One body came back half-melted, like something had tried to compost him.” |
48|| 4 | “Tiny slaad tadpoles have been seen carrying scraps toward the old greenhouse.” |
49|| 5 | “Fire scares them. Or maybe it just makes them angry.” |
50|| 6 | “The greenhouse was sealed after the last crop failed. Nobody remembers who locked it.”
51|
52|---
53|
54|### Rumors
55|
56|The characters may hear one or more of the following rumors before reaching the greenhouse:
57|
58|| d6 | Rumor |
59||---:|---|
60|| 1 | “The plants move after sunset. I saw vines dragging a goat uphill.” |
61|| 2 | “There’s croaking in the irrigation channels, but no frogs in the fields anymore.” |
62|| 3 | “One body came back half-melted, like something had tried to compost him.” |
63|| 4 | “Tiny slaad tadpoles have been seen carrying scraps toward the old greenhouse.” |
64|| 5 | “Fire scares them. Or maybe it just makes them angry.” |
65|| 6 | “The greenhouse was sealed after the last crop failed. Nobody remembers who locked it.” |
66|
67|---
68|
69|# Part 1: Investigation
70|
71|*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*
72|
73|Part 1 begins when the characters arrive at the damaged farmstead in [[Astallon Acres]]. They investigate the missing livestock and workers, inspect the corrupted Arcannabis fields, and follow signs toward the abandoned greenhouse near [[Zooka Mire]]. They do not need to discover every clue. Two or three successful investigation scenes are enough to point them toward the Outer Nest.
74|
75|Read or paraphrase:
76|
77|> The air grows wet and green as you approach the infected ground. Leaves shine with a greasy film, and the soil gives slightly beneath each step, as though the earth itself has gone soft.
78|>
79|> Somewhere ahead, something croaks.
80|>
81|> Then something smaller croaks back.
82|
83|## Investigation Scenes
84|
85|## Investigation Scenes
86|
87|Use two or three of the following scenes. Each scene should provide a clue even if the characters fail a check. A failed check may cost time, attract attention, or create a later complication.
88|
89|### Frightened Locals
90|
91|Witnesses describe missing livestock, moving plants, strange croaking, and small creatures dragging food into the brush.
92|
93|**Useful Checks:**
94|
95|- **DC 11 Charisma (Persuasion):** Calm witnesses and get a clear description.
96|- **DC 11 Wisdom (Insight):** Notice that witnesses are more frightened by the croaking than by the plants.
97|- **DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation):** Piece together that the disappearances are spreading outward from one central site.
98|
99|**Clue:** The creatures are collecting food rather than merely attacking at random.
100|
101|### Damaged Crops or Bodies
102|
103|The party finds ruined crops, slime-burned fences, half-eaten livestock, or a partially dissolved corpse.
104|
105|**Useful Checks:**
106|
107|- **DC 11 Intelligence (Nature):** Identify that the plants are growing too quickly and feeding on organic remains.
108|- **DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine):** Determine that acid or digestive slime caused the injuries.
109|- **DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana):** Sense planar or chaotic magic in the residue.
110|
111|**Clue:** The infestation is both botanical and extraplanar, and it is converting organic matter into growth.
112|
113|### Slime Trail
114|
115|A slick trail leads toward the nest. Tiny webbed prints and dragged scraps of food mark the path.
116|
117|**Useful Checks:**
118|
119|- **DC 11 Wisdom (Survival):** Follow the trail.
120|- **DC 13 Wisdom (Perception):** Spot hidden tadpoles watching from the brush.
121|- **DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth):** Approach without alerting the outer nest.
122|
123|**Clue:** The trail leads toward an overgrown structure, drainage tunnel, or root-choked hollow where the creatures are nesting.
124|
125|## Clues
126|
127|Reward good investigation with one or more of the following clues:
128|
129|- The smaller creatures are spawn and will defend egg clusters.
130|- A larger creature protects the tadpoles at all costs.
131|- Fire frightens or disrupts the plant growth.
132|- The lair has hidden entrances through roots, drains, or burrows.
133|- The nest is feeding on victims to grow more spawn.
134|- The infestation is spreading outward from a central chamber.
135|
136|Once the characters have enough information, proceed to Part 2.
137|
138|---
139|
140|# Part 2: The Outer Nest
141|
142|*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*
143|## Encounter: Slaad Tadpoles
144|The characters enter the infected area. This section establishes the danger and drains a few resources without overshadowing the final encounter.
145|
146|Read or paraphrase:
147|
148|> The path disappears beneath thick vines and glossy leaves. Bulging pods hang from branches like wet fruit. Greenish slime trembles in shallow puddles whenever something croaks nearby.
149|>
150|> Small shapes move beneath the leaves.
151|>
152|> One of them stops.
153|>
154|> Then all of them start croaking at once.
155|
156|## Encounter: Salad Tadpoles
157|
158|Use **4–8 Salad Tadpoles**, depending on party size and remaining resources. The tadpoles harass the party, retreat through small gaps, and try to draw intruders toward hazards rather than fight to the death.
159|
160|If custom statistics are unavailable, use low-CR frog, twig blight, or crawling claw-style creatures and describe their attacks as acidic, poisonous, or vine-based.
161|
162|The tadpoles should reveal the nest’s behavior during this encounter. They defend routes to the inner chambers, but they prioritize sounding alarms and protecting egg clusters over killing intruders.
163|
164|## Outer Nest Hazards
165|
166|Choose or roll one hazard. A hazard can occur during the tadpole encounter or immediately afterward.
167|
168|| d4 | Hazard |
169||---:|---|
170|| 1 | **Acidic Pollen.** A disturbed pod bursts. Creatures within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take acid damage and cough loudly, alerting the nest. |
171|| 2 | **Grasping Vines.** Vines turn the area into difficult terrain. A creature that dashes must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. |
172|| 3 | **Slime Sink.** A patch of ground collapses into digestive muck. A creature that enters it must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or become restrained until freed. |
173|| 4 | **Croaking Alarm.** Tadpoles begin a rhythmic chorus. If they are not stopped within 2 rounds, the Red Salad is alert during the final encounter and cannot be surprised. |
174|
175|---
176|
177|# Part 3: The Heart of the Nest
178|
179|*Estimated Duration: 60–75 minutes*
180|
181|The heart of the nest is a wet chamber, greenhouse, root cellar, sewer dome, or druidic hollow filled with egg sacs and nutrient slime. Choose details that fit the location established during the investigation.
182|
183|Read or paraphrase:
184|
185|> The nest opens before you in a pulse of wet heat and sour green stink. Egg sacs cling to roots and cracked stone. Slime pools bubble between heaps of bones, tools, boots, and half-digested packs.
186|>
187|> At the center of it all squats something red, swollen, and alive with twitching leaves. Its throat inflates.
188|>
189|> The whole chamber croaks back.
190|
191|## Boss Encounter
192|
193|Enemies:
194|
195|- **1 Red Salad**
196|- **Several Salad Tadpoles**
197|
198|If custom statistics are unavailable, use a suitable plant, frog, or slaad-like stat block for the Red Salad and reskin its attacks with acid, vines, and tongue strikes.
199|
200|The final encounter has three simultaneous objectives: defeat the Red Salad, prevent more tadpoles from hatching, and stop the creature from escaping into the surrounding area.
201|
202|## Egg Clusters
203|
204|Place **3 egg clusters** around the battlefield.
205|
206|- Each egg cluster has AC 10 and 10 hit points.
207|- Fire damage destroys an egg cluster immediately.
208|- At the end of every other round, one intact egg cluster hatches **1 Salad Tadpole**.
209|- Destroying all egg clusters stops new tadpoles from appearing.
210|
211|## Red Salad Tactics
212|
213|The Red Salad is protective and territorial.
214|
215|- It prioritizes characters attacking egg clusters.
216|- It uses tadpoles and terrain to slow enemies.
217|- It retreats toward underground tunnels if reduced to low hit points.
218|- Once per fight, it may consume a nearby tadpole or egg cluster to regain hit points.
219|- If escape is possible, it tries to reach a secondary chamber rather than fight in an exposed area.
220|
221|## Battlefield Features
222|
223|| Feature | Effect |
224||---|---|
225|| Acid Pools | A creature that enters a pool or starts its turn there takes acid damage. |
226|| Hanging Vines | Provide half cover and can be cut or burned. |
227|| Nutrient Slime | Plant creatures that start their turn in the slime regain a small amount of hit points. |
228|| Rotten Walkways | A creature that takes heavy damage while standing on one may need to save or fall. |
229|| Egg Sacs | Hatch tadpoles if ignored. |
230|
231|## Objectives Beyond Killing Everything
232|
233|The characters may also:
234|
235|- Destroy the egg clusters.
236|- Rescue an NPC wrapped in roots.
237|- Prevent the Red Salad from escaping into underground tunnels.
238|- Recover the strange seed or planar spore at the heart of the nest.
239|- Secure samples without allowing the infestation to spread.
240|
241|---
242|
243|# Part 4: Conclusion
244|
245|*Estimated Duration: 30 minutes*
246|
247|When the Red Salad is defeated and the egg clusters are destroyed, the infestation begins to collapse. Vines loosen, slime pools dry into crust, and the constant croaking finally stops.
248|
249|If the characters do not destroy the egg clusters, the infestation survives even if the Red Salad dies. The surviving spawn may retreat into drains, roots, or nearby farmland.
250|
251|## Possible Rewards
252|
253|- Payment from the employer.
254|- Harvested monster parts using [[Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting]].
255|- A strange magical seed or planar spore.
256|- Acid glands, sticky slime, or volatile spores.
257|- A clue pointing toward another infestation.
258|- Gratitude from farmers, apothecaries, or local residents.
259|
260|## Lingering Consequences
261|
262|Choose one or more:
263|
264|- A surviving tadpole escapes into the drainage system.
265|- The strange seed remains valuable but faintly alive.
266|- Infected soil can be purified, sold, studied, or misused.
267|- A faction wants the remains for research.
268|- Someone insists the infestation was not an accident.
269|- Destroying the nest releases a burst of planar energy that mutates nearby plants.
270|
271|---
272|
273|# Difficulty
274|
275|For **four to five 3rd-level characters**, use the following progression:
276|
277|| Encounter | Difficulty |
278||---|---|
279|| Investigation obstacle | Easy |
280|| Outer Nest tadpoles and hazard | Medium |
281|| Optional hazard or ambush | Easy–Medium |
282|| Red Salad and tadpoles | Hard |
283|
284|The final fight is usually sufficient if the party has already spent some spells, hit points, or class resources in the Outer Nest.
285|
286|---
287|
288|# DM Notes
289|
290|## Tone
291|
292|Keep the adventure swampy, gross, and strange rather than relentlessly grim. The danger should feel real, but the creature’s behavior can remain bizarre and darkly funny. Emphasize coordinated tadpoles, absurdly wet vegetation, sour smells, and the unsettling transformation of victims into fertilizer.
293|
294|## Scaling
295|
296|- For a weaker party, use fewer tadpoles, reduce the number of egg clusters to two, and remove one battlefield hazard.
297|- For a stronger party, add tadpoles, allow two egg clusters to hatch at once, or give the Red Salad an additional use of its strongest ability.
298|- For a shorter session, skip the Outer Nest combat and use one investigation hazard before the boss.
299|- For a longer session, add a trapped NPC, rival hunters, or a faction trying to steal samples.
300|
301|## Harvest Ideas
302|
303|- Red Salad tongue
304|- Acidic digestive slime
305|- Slaad-touched seed
306|- Tadpole glands
307|- Egg cluster membrane
308|- Planar compost

## Boss Encounter

Enemies:

- **1 Red Slaad**
- **Several Slaad Tadpoles**

Use the official **Red Slaad** and **Slaad Tadpole** stat blocks from the 5.5e *Monster Manual*. Do not use custom Salad or frog-plant creature statistics.

The final encounter has three simultaneous objectives: defeat the Red Slaad, prevent more tadpoles from hatching, and stop the creature from escaping into the surrounding area.

## Egg Clusters

Place **3 egg clusters** around the battlefield.

- Each egg cluster has AC 10 and 10 hit points.
- Fire damage destroys an egg cluster immediately.
- At the end of every other round, one intact egg cluster hatches **1 Slaad Tadpole**.
- Destroying all egg clusters stops new tadpoles from appearing.

## Red Slaad Tactics

The Red Slaad is protective and territorial.

- It prioritizes characters attacking egg clusters.
- It uses Slaad Tadpoles and terrain to slow enemies.
- It retreats toward underground tunnels if reduced to low hit points.
- Once per fight, it may consume a nearby Slaad Tadpole or egg cluster to regain hit points.
- If escape is possible, it tries to reach a secondary chamber rather than fight in an exposed area.

value.newText:
# Part 4: Conclusion

*Estimated Duration: 30 minutes*

When the Red Slaad is defeated and the egg clusters are destroyed, the infestation begins to collapse. Vines loosen, slime pools dry into crust, and the constant croaking finally stops.

If the characters do not destroy the egg clusters, the infestation survives even if the Red Slaad dies. The surviving Slaad Tadpoles may retreat into drains, roots, or nearby farmland.

## Possible Rewards

- Payment from the employer.
- Harvested monster parts using [[Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting]].
- A strange magical seed or planar spore.
- Acid glands, sticky slime, or volatile spores.
- A clue pointing toward another infestation.
- Gratitude from farmers, apothecaries, or local residents.

## Lingering Consequences

Choose one or more:

- A surviving Slaad Tadpole escapes into the drainage system.
- The strange seed remains valuable but faintly alive.
- Infected soil can be purified, sold, studied, or misused.
- A faction wants the remains for research.
- Someone insists the infestation was not an accident.
- Destroying the nest releases a burst of planar energy that mutates nearby plants.

---

# Difficulty

For **four to five 3rd-level characters**, use the following progression:

| Encounter | Difficulty |
|---|---|
| Investigation obstacle | Easy |
| Outer Nest Slaad Tadpoles and hazard | Medium |
| Optional hazard or ambush | Easy–Medium |
| Red Slaad and Slaad Tadpoles | Hard |

The final fight is usually sufficient if the party has already spent some spells, hit points, or class resources in the Outer Nest.

---

# DM Notes

## Tone

Keep the adventure swampy, gross, and strange rather than relentlessly grim. The danger should feel real, but the Slaad’s behavior can remain bizarre and darkly funny. Emphasize coordinated Slaad Tadpoles, absurdly wet vegetation, sour smells, and the unsettling transformation of victims into fertilizer.

## Scaling

- For a weaker party, use fewer Slaad Tadpoles, reduce the number of egg clusters to two, and remove one battlefield hazard.
- For a stronger party, add Slaad Tadpoles, allow two egg clusters to hatch at once, or give the Red Slaad an additional use of its strongest ability.
- For a shorter session, skip the Outer Nest combat and use one investigation hazard before the boss.
- For a longer session, add a trapped NPC, rival hunters, or a faction trying to steal samples.

## Harvest Ideas

- Red Slaad tongue
- Acidic digestive slime
- Slaad-touched seed
- Slaad Tadpole glands
- Egg cluster membrane
- Planar compost

*Estimated Duration: 30 minutes*

When the Red Slaad is defeated and the egg clusters are destroyed, the infestation begins to collapse. Vines loosen, slime pools dry into crust, and the constant croaking finally stops.

If the characters do not destroy the egg clusters, the infestation survives even if the Red Slaad dies. The surviving Slaad Tadpoles may retreat into drains, roots, or nearby farmland.

## Possible Rewards

- Payment from the employer.
- Harvested monster parts using [[Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting]].
- A strange magical seed or planar spore.
- Acid glands, sticky slime, or volatile spores.
- A clue pointing toward another infestation.
- Gratitude from farmers, apothecaries, or local residents.

## Lingering Consequences

Choose one or more:

- A surviving Slaad Tadpole escapes into the drainage system.
- The strange seed remains valuable but faintly alive.
- Infected soil can be purified, sold, studied, or misused.
- A faction wants the remains for research.
- Someone insists the infestation was not an accident.
- Destroying the nest releases a burst of planar energy that mutates nearby plants.

---

# Difficulty

For **four to five 3rd-level characters**, use the following progression:

| Encounter | Difficulty |
|---|---|
| Investigation obstacle | Easy |
| Outer Nest Slaad Tadpoles and hazard | Medium |
| Optional hazard or ambush | Easy–Medium |
| Red Slaad and Slaad Tadpoles | Hard |

The final fight is usually sufficient if the party has already spent some spells, hit points, or class resources in the Outer Nest.

---

# DM Notes

## Tone

Keep the adventure swampy, gross, and strange rather than relentlessly grim. The danger should feel real, but the Slaad’s behavior can remain bizarre and darkly funny. Emphasize coordinated Slaad Tadpoles, absurdly wet vegetation, sour smells, and the unsettling transformation of victims into fertilizer.

## Scaling

- For a weaker party, use fewer Slaad Tadpoles, reduce the number of egg clusters to two, and remove one battlefield hazard.
- For a stronger party, add Slaad Tadpoles, allow two egg clusters to hatch at once, or give the Red Slaad an additional use of its strongest ability.
- For a shorter session, skip the Outer Nest combat and use one investigation hazard before the boss.
- For a longer session, add a trapped NPC, rival hunters, or a faction trying to steal samples.

## Harvest Ideas

- Red Slaad tongue
- Acidic digestive slime
- Slaad-touched seed
- Slaad Tadpole glands
- Egg cluster membrane
- Planar compost
"}

value.newText:
## Boss Encounter

Enemies:

- **1 Red Slaad**
- **Several Slaad Tadpoles**

Use the official **Red Slaad** and **Slaad Tadpole** stat blocks from the 5.5e *Monster Manual*. Do not use custom Salad or frog-plant creature statistics.

The final encounter has three simultaneous objectives: defeat the Red Slaad, prevent more tadpoles from hatching, and stop the creature from escaping into the surrounding area.

## Egg Clusters

Place **3 egg clusters** around the battlefield.

- Each egg cluster has AC 10 and 10 hit points.
- Fire damage destroys an egg cluster immediately.
- At the end of every other round, one intact egg cluster hatches **1 Slaad Tadpole**.
- Destroying all egg clusters stops new tadpoles from appearing.

## Red Slaad Tactics

The Red Slaad is protective and territorial.

- It prioritizes characters attacking egg clusters.
- It uses Slaad Tadpoles and terrain to slow enemies.
- It retreats toward underground tunnels if reduced to low hit points.
- Once per fight, it may consume a nearby Slaad Tadpole or egg cluster to regain hit points.
- If escape is possible, it tries to reach a secondary chamber rather than fight in an exposed area.

## Battlefield Features

      "content": "1|*A Tier 1 Free League of Stickyickistan adventure for four to five 3rd-level characters*
2|
3|# Introduction
4|
5|**Curse of Slaad** is a short monster-hunt adventure set in [[Stickyickistan]] and designed for a three- to four-hour session. The characters investigate disappearances and corrupted crops in [[North Booftown]], the city-state’s agricultural heartland. The infestation begins near [[Astallon Acres]], along the wetlands bordering [[Zooka Mire]], and threatens the region’s livestock, farm workers, and [[Arcannabis]] fields.
6|
7|The adventure is intended to feel like swampy horror-comedy: gross, weird, dangerous, and slightly ridiculous. Emphasize wet croaks, twitching vegetation, sour compost smells, and the unsettling sight of tiny frog-things working together.
8|
9|## Adventure Background
10|
11|The infestation began when contaminated [[Arcannabis]] fertilizer was dumped near an abandoned agricultural greenhouse on the edge of [[Astallon Acres]]. A planar spore within the waste infected the greenhouse’s irrigation system, mutating the plants and creating the first slaad tadpoles. The residue at the heart of the nest can later reveal whether the contamination was accidental or deliberate.
12|
13|At the center of the infestation is a **Red Slaad**, a violent extraplanar predator that protects its spawn and feeds victims into the nest. Unless the infestation is stopped, the slaad will spread through the farms of [[North Booftown]], into [[Zooka Mire]], and eventually toward Stickyickistan’s food and Arcannabis production.
14|
15|## Adventure Hook
16|
17|The adventure begins when the characters are hired by [[Ezra Astallon]], the wealthy owner of [[Astallon Acres]]. His workers have reported missing livestock, corrupted crops, and two missing farmhands near an abandoned agricultural greenhouse. Ezra wants the problem solved before it damages his harvest or attracts the attention of the [[Nevercough Tribunal]].
18|
19|After accepting the job, the characters travel into [[North Booftown]] and begin Part 1 when they arrive at the first damaged farmstead.
20|
21|### Opening Scene
22|
23|Read or paraphrase:
24|
25|> The farmstead lies at the edge of [[Astallon Acres]], where cultivated fields give way to wet ground and tangled reeds. Rows of Arcannabis plants lean toward the road, their leaves swollen and darkened with a greasy green film.
26|>
27|> The livestock pens stand open and empty. A broken fence disappears beneath a mat of vines, and something wet has dragged a furrow through the mud toward the distant wetlands.
28|>
29|> [[Ezra Astallon]] waits beside the farmhouse, dressed too well for the mud and speaking in a low, impatient voice.
30|>
31|> “The animals vanished first. Then two workers went looking for them. The crops began changing yesterday. If this reaches the rest of North Booftown, we could lose half the harvest.”
32|>
33|> From beyond the fields, something croaks.
34|>
35|> A smaller voice answers from somewhere beneath the reeds.
36|
37|Ezra provides the characters with directions to the abandoned greenhouse and promises payment for stopping the infestation. The characters then begin Part 1 by interviewing farm workers, examining the damaged crops, or following the first slime trail.
38|
39|### Rumors
40|
41|The characters may hear one or more of the following rumors before reaching the greenhouse:
42|
43|| d6 | Rumor |
44||---:|---|
45|| 1 | “The plants move after sunset. I saw vines dragging a goat uphill.” |
46|| 2 | “There’s croaking in the irrigation channels, but no frogs in the fields anymore.” |
47|| 3 | “One body came back half-melted, like something had tried to compost him.” |
48|| 4 | “Tiny slaad tadpoles have been seen carrying scraps toward the old greenhouse.” |
49|| 5 | “Fire scares them. Or maybe it just makes them angry.” |
50|| 6 | “The greenhouse was sealed after the last crop failed. Nobody remembers who locked it.” |
51|
52|---
53|
54|# Part 1: Investigation
55|
56|*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*
57|
58|Part 1 begins when the characters arrive at the damaged farmstead in [[Astallon Acres]]. They investigate the missing livestock and workers, inspect the corrupted Arcannabis fields, and follow signs toward the abandoned greenhouse near [[Zooka Mire]]. They do not need to discover every clue. Two or three successful investigation scenes are enough to point them toward the Outer Nest.
59|
60|Read or paraphrase:
61|
62|> The air grows wet and green as you approach the infected ground. Leaves shine with a greasy film, and the soil gives slightly beneath each step, as though the earth itself has gone soft.
63|>
64|> Somewhere ahead, something croaks.
65|>
66|> Then something smaller croaks back.
67|
68|## Investigation Scenes
69|
70|Use two or three of the following scenes. Each scene should provide a clue even if the characters fail a check. A failed check may cost time, attract attention, or create a later complication.
71|
72|### Frightened Locals
73|
74|Witnesses describe missing livestock, moving plants, strange croaking, and small creatures dragging food into the brush.
75|
76|**Useful Checks:**
77|
78|- **DC 11 Charisma (Persuasion):** Calm witnesses and get a clear description.
79|- **DC 11 Wisdom (Insight):** Notice that witnesses are more frightened by the croaking than by the plants.
80|- **DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation):** Piece together that the disappearances are spreading outward from one central site.
81|
82|**Clue:** The creatures are collecting food rather than merely attacking at random.
83|
84|### Damaged Crops or Bodies
85|
86|The party finds ruined crops, slime-burned fences, half-eaten livestock, or a partially dissolved corpse.
87|
88|**Useful Checks:**
89|
90|- **DC 11 Intelligence (Nature):** Identify that the plants are growing too quickly and feeding on organic remains.
91|- **DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine):** Determine that acid or digestive slime caused the injuries.
92|- **DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana):** Sense planar or chaotic magic in the residue.
93|
94|**Clue:** The infestation is both botanical and extraplanar, and it is converting organic matter into growth.
95|
96|### Slime Trail
97|
98|A slick trail leads toward the nest. Tiny webbed prints and dragged scraps of food mark the path.
99|
100|**Useful Checks:**
101|
102|- **DC 11 Wisdom (Survival):** Follow the trail.
103|- **DC 13 Wisdom (Perception):** Spot hidden tadpoles watching from the brush.
104|- **DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth):** Approach without alerting the outer nest.
105|
106|**Clue:** The trail leads toward an overgrown structure, drainage tunnel, or root-choked hollow where the creatures are nesting.
107|
108|## Clues
109|
110|Reward good investigation with one or more of the following clues:
111|
112|- The smaller creatures are spawn and will defend egg clusters.
113|- A larger creature protects the tadpoles at all costs.
114|- Fire frightens or disrupts the plant growth.
115|- The lair has hidden entrances through roots, drains, or burrows.
116|- The nest is feeding on victims to grow more spawn.
117|- The infestation is spreading outward from a central chamber.
118|
119|Once the characters have enough information, proceed to Part 2.
120|
121|---
122|
123|# Part 2: The Outer Nest
124|
125|*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*
126|## Encounter: Slaad Tadpoles
127|The characters enter the infected area. This section establishes the danger and drains a few resources without overshadowing the final encounter.
128|
129|Read or paraphrase:
130|
131|> The path disappears beneath thick vines and glossy leaves. Bulging pods hang from branches like wet fruit. Greenish slime trembles in shallow puddles whenever something croaks nearby.
132|>
133|> Small shapes move beneath the leaves.
134|>
135|> One of them stops.
136|>
137|> Then all of them start croaking at once.
138|
139|## Encounter: Salad Tadpoles
140|## Encounter: Slaad Tadpoles
141|Use **4–8 Salad Tadpoles**, depending on party size and remaining resources. The tadpoles harass the party, retreat through small gaps, and try to draw intruders toward hazards rather than fight to the death.
142|
143|If custom statistics are unavailable, use low-CR frog, twig blight, or crawling claw-style creatures and describe their attacks as acidic, poisonous, or vine-based.
144|
145|The tadpoles should reveal the nest’s behavior during this encounter. They defend routes to the inner chambers, but they prioritize sounding alarms and protecting egg clusters over killing intruders.
146|
147|## Outer Nest Hazards
148|
149|Choose or roll one hazard. A hazard can occur during the tadpole encounter or immediately afterward.
150|
151|| d4 | Hazard |
152||---:|---|
153|| 1 | **Acidic Pollen.** A disturbed pod bursts. Creatures within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take acid damage and cough loudly, alerting the nest. |
154|| 2 | **Grasping Vines.** Vines turn the area into difficult terrain. A creature that dashes must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. |
155|| 3 | **Slime Sink.** A patch of ground collapses into digestive muck. A creature that enters it must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or become restrained until freed. |

160|# Part 3: The Heart of the Nest
161|
162|*Estimated Duration: 60–75 minutes*
163|
164|The heart of the nest is a wet chamber, greenhouse, root cellar, sewer dome, or druidic hollow filled with egg sacs and nutrient slime. Choose details that fit the location established during the investigation.
165|
166|Read or paraphrase:

168|> The nest opens before you in a pulse of wet heat and sour green stink. Egg sacs cling to roots and cracked stone. Slime pools bubble between heaps of bones, tools, boots, and half-digested packs.

# Part 2: The Outer Nest

*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*

The characters enter the infected greenhouse and its surrounding irrigation channels. This section establishes the danger and drains a few resources without overshadowing the final encounter.

## Encounter: Slaad Tadpoles

Read or paraphrase:

> The path disappears beneath thick vines and glossy leaves. Bulging pods hang from the greenhouse rafters like wet fruit. Greenish slime trembles in shallow irrigation channels whenever something croaks nearby.
>
> Small shapes move beneath the leaves.
>
> One of them stops.
>
> Then all of them start croaking at once.

Use **4–8 Slaad Tadpoles**, depending on party size and remaining resources. The tadpoles harass the party, retreat through small gaps, and try to draw intruders toward hazards rather than fight to the death.

The tadpoles defend routes to the inner chamber, but they prioritize sounding alarms and protecting the egg clusters over killing intruders.

## Outer Nest Hazards

Choose or roll one hazard during the tadpole encounter or immediately afterward.

| d4 | Hazard |
|---:|---|
| 1 | **Acidic Pollen.** A disturbed pod bursts. Creatures within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take acid damage and cough loudly, alerting the nest. |
| 2 | **Grasping Vines.** Vines turn the area into difficult terrain. A creature that dashes must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. |
| 3 | **Slime Sink.** A patch of ground collapses into digestive muck. A creature that enters it must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or become restrained until freed. |
| 4 | **Croaking Alarm.** The tadpoles begin a rhythmic chorus. If they are not stopped within 2 rounds, the Red Slaad is alert during the final encounter and cannot be surprised. |

---

# Part 3: The Heart of the Nest

*Estimated Duration: 60–75 minutes*

The heart of the nest lies beneath the greenhouse in a flooded root cellar connected to the old irrigation system. The chamber is filled with egg clusters, nutrient slime, and the remains of the creatures and workers consumed by the infestation.

Read or paraphrase:

> The greenhouse floor gives way to a flooded chamber beneath the roots. Egg sacs cling to cracked stone and rusted irrigation pipes. Slime pools bubble between heaps of bones, tools, boots, and half-digested packs.
>
> At the center of the chamber stands a tall, red-skinned creature with a frog-like head and long claws. It turns toward you, its throat inflating as it prepares to croak.
>
> The whole chamber answers.

## Boss Encounter

Enemies:

- **1 Red Slaad**
- **Several Slaad Tadpoles**

Use the official **Red Slaad** and **Slaad Tadpole** stat blocks from the 5.5e *Monster Manual*. The final encounter has three objectives: defeat the Red Slaad, prevent more tadpoles from hatching, and stop the creature from escaping into the surrounding farmland.

## Egg Clusters

Place **3 egg clusters** around the battlefield.

- Each egg cluster has AC 10 and 10 hit points.
- Fire damage destroys an egg cluster immediately.
- At the end of every other round, one intact egg cluster hatches **1 Slaad Tadpole**.
- Destroying all egg clusters stops new tadpoles from appearing.

## Red Slaad Tactics

The Red Slaad is protective and territorial.

- It prioritizes characters attacking egg clusters.
- It uses Slaad Tadpoles and terrain to slow enemies.
- It retreats toward the greenhouse tunnels if reduced to low hit points.
- Once per fight, it may consume a nearby Slaad Tadpole or egg cluster to regain hit points.
- If escape is possible, it tries to reach the irrigation channels and spread the infestation into the surrounding farms.

## Battlefield Features

| Feature | Effect |
|---|---|
| Acid Pools | A creature that enters a pool or starts its turn there takes acid damage. |
| Hanging Vines | Provide half cover and can be cut or burned. |
| Nutrient Slime | A creature that starts its turn in the slime regains a small amount of hit points. |
| Rotten Walkways | A creature that takes heavy damage while standing on one may need to save or fall. |
| Egg Sacs | Hatch Slaad Tadpoles if ignored. |

## Objectives Beyond Killing Everything

The characters may also:

- Destroy the egg clusters.
- Rescue a missing farmhand wrapped in roots.
- Prevent the Red Slaad from escaping into the irrigation system.
- Recover the planar spore at the heart of the nest.
- Secure samples without allowing the infestation to spread.

---

# Part 4: Conclusion

*Estimated Duration: 30 minutes*

When the Red Slaad is defeated and the egg clusters are destroyed, the infestation begins to collapse. Vines loosen, slime pools dry into crust, and the constant croaking finally stops.

If the characters do not destroy the egg clusters, the infestation survives even if the Red Slaad dies. Surviving Slaad Tadpoles may retreat into the irrigation system, drains, or nearby farmland.

## Possible Rewards

- Payment from [[Ezra Astallon]].
- Harvested monster parts using [[Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting]].
- The planar spore, if recovered intact.
- Acid glands, sticky slime, or volatile residue from the infestation.
- A clue identifying the source of the contaminated fertilizer.
- Ezra’s gratitude and continued access to Astallon Acres.

## Lingering Consequences

- A surviving Slaad Tadpole escapes into the irrigation system.
- The planar spore remains valuable but faintly alive.
- Infected soil can be purified, sold, studied, or misused.
- A faction discovers the infestation and seeks to recover the spore.
- Destroying the nest releases a burst of planar energy that mutates nearby plants.

---

# Difficulty

For **four to five 3rd-level characters**, use the following progression:

| Encounter | Difficulty |
|---|---|
| Investigation obstacle | Easy |
| Outer Nest Slaad Tadpoles and hazard | Medium |
| Red Slaad and Slaad Tadpoles | Hard |

The final fight is usually sufficient if the party has already spent some spells, hit points, or class resources in the Outer Nest.

---

# DM Notes

## Tone

Keep the adventure swampy, gross, and strange rather than relentlessly grim. The danger should feel real, but the Slaad’s behavior can remain bizarre and darkly funny. Emphasize coordinated Slaad Tadpoles, wet vegetation, sour smells, and the unsettling transformation of victims into fertilizer.

## Scaling

- For a weaker party, use fewer Slaad Tadpoles, reduce the number of egg clusters to two, and remove one battlefield hazard.
- For a stronger party, add Slaad Tadpoles, allow two egg clusters to hatch at once, or give the Red Slaad an additional use of its strongest ability.
- For a shorter session, skip the Outer Nest combat and use one investigation hazard before the boss.
- For a longer session, add a rival salvage crew trying to steal the planar spore.

## Harvest Ideas

- Red Slaad tongue
- Acidic digestive slime
- Planar spore
- Slaad Tadpole glands
- Egg cluster membrane
- Contaminated Arcannabis fertilizer

      "content": "1|**The Rolling Papers** is Stickyickistan’s most widely circulated newspaper, equal parts investigative journalism, rumor mill, scandal sheet, and rolling tray liner. Its reporters chase stories across taverns, trade roads, noble courts, dungeon entrances, and suspiciously smoking back alleys, publishing whatever they can verify, mostly verify, or at least make entertaining.
2|
3|The paper is famous for bold headlines, anonymous sources, dramatic woodcut illustrations, and a surprisingly consistent record of being right about things no one wanted printed. Adventurers often find their exploits exaggerated in its pages, while villains, politicians, Guildmasters, and minor gods dread seeing their names above the fold.
4|
5|Its motto is simple:
6|
7|> **“If it burns, bleeds, or blazes, it belongs in The Rolling Papers.”**
8|
9|# What Gets Posted Here
10|
11|Use **The Rolling Papers** for adventure hooks involving:
12|
13|- Public contracts.
14|- Legal bounty work.
15|- Festival security.
16|- Caravan guard jobs on official roads.
17|- Missing persons notices.
18|- Monster attacks near towns, farms, roads, or trade routes.
19|- Civic emergencies.
20|- Noble announcements and public scandals.
21|- Guild postings with proper paperwork.
22|- Temple requests, relief efforts, and charity drives.
23|- Investigations where witnesses are expected to talk openly.
24|- Jobs where the employer is comfortable being named in print.
25|- Problems the authorities know about, tolerate, or actively want solved.
26|
27|If a job requires secrecy, fake names, bribes, contraband, sabotage, theft, or the phrase “do not involve the authorities,” it probably belongs in [[The Roach Clip]] instead.
28|
29|# Rolling Papers Adventure Advertisement Template
30|
31|DMs can advertise upcoming Free League adventures as notices, classifieds, or dramatic front-page warnings in **The Rolling Papers**.
32|
33|Use the following template when posting an adventure ad:
34|
35|```markdown

37|

40|**Recommended Level:** [Character level or range]

42|**Tone:** [Comedy, horror, mystery, heroic fantasy, dungeon crawl, political chaos, etc.]  
43|**Location:** [Where the adventure begins or takes place]  
44|
45|### Headline
46|
47|> [Write the dramatic Rolling Papers headline here.]
48|
49|### Public Notice
50|
51|[Write the in-universe ad, rumor, job posting, warning, wanted notice, classified, or article hook that characters would see.]
52|

56|- **Combat / roleplay / exploration mix:** [Example: Combat-heavy, social mystery, balanced, exploration-focused.]

73|# Example: Monsters at the Northbourne Orchard Festival
74|
75|**Posted by:** [[Lady Isolde Northbourne]]  
76|**DM:** Initiate of Tribulation, Vorg Lordcaster
77|**Tier:** Tier 1  
78|**Recommended Level:** 3 - 4  
79|**Expected Length:** ~4 hours 
80|**Tone:** Public festival trouble, monster hunt, light investigation  
81|**Location:** [[House Northbourne]] holdings  
82|
83|### Headline
84|
85|> **Northbourne Harvest Committee Seeks Licensed Adventurers After Prize Pumpkins Bite Back**
86|
87|### Public Notice
88|
89|The annual Northbourne Orchard Festival is seeking capable adventurers to provide lawful security, investigate unusual disturbances, and protect guests after several prize vegetables, decorative scarecrows, and at least one cider barrel displayed signs of hostile animation.
90|
91|Representatives of [[House Northbourne]] insist the festival remains open, safe, and family friendly, provided no one enters the eastern pumpkin rows without an escort.
92|
93|Interested adventurers should report to [[Lady Isolde Northbourne]] for guard assignments, hazard pay, and a complimentary festival ribbon.
94|
95|### What Players Should Know
96|
97|- **Content / vibe:** Public festival chaos, animated produce, rural mystery, light horror-comedy.
98|- **Combat / roleplay / exploration mix:** Balanced, with social scenes, investigation, and likely combat in the orchard.
99|- **Character hooks:** Good for monster hunters, local heroes, guards for hire, nobles, food lovers, or anyone seeking legitimate public work.
100|- **Special notes:** This is an above-the-board contract. Characters are expected to protect civilians, avoid property damage when possible, and not steal from festival vendors.
101|
102|### Rewards Teaser
103|
104|The festival committee offers coin, public goodwill with [[House Northbourne]], and possible access to rare seasonal goods.
105|
106|### Sign-Up
107|
108|**DM:** Chase  
109|**Date / Time:** TBD  
110|**Seats:** 4 - 5 players  
111|**How to join:** Post in the Free League chat.

      "content": "1|**The Roach Clip** is the under-the-table counterpart to [[The Rolling Papers]]: a whispered classifieds network for jobs too illegal, embarrassing, dangerous, politically inconvenient, or cursed to print in a respectable newspaper.

4|
5|Most postings are anonymous, half-true, and written by people who absolutely do not want the road authorities, noble houses, temple auditors, guild inspectors, or rival criminals asking questions.

67|# Example: Smoke on the Silt Road
68|
69|**Posted by:** A Concerned Freight Owner  
70|**DM:** Initiate of Tribulation, Vorg Lordcaster  
71|**Tier:** Tier 1  
72|**Recommended Level:** 3 - 4  
73|**Expected Length:** ~4 hours  
74|**Tone:** Roadside crime, caravan trouble, Arcannabis weirdness  
75|**Location:** [[The Silt Road]]  
76|**Legality:** Gray trending rapidly toward illegal  
77|
78|### Coded Notice
79|
80|> **Need discreet hands for cargo retrieval. Shipment delayed. Cargo temperamental. Do not involve road authorities. Do not open anything marked with blue twine. Payment upon silence.**
81|
82|### Public-Facing Job Pitch
83|
84|A private freight owner is seeking capable, discreet adventurers to recover delayed cargo from a troublesome stretch of [[The Silt Road]]. The employer claims the matter is time-sensitive, reputationally delicate, and “not worth bothering officials over.”
85|
86|The job requires finding the shipment, confirming its condition, and ensuring it reaches the correct recipient without unnecessary attention.
87|
88|### What Players Should Know
89|
90|- **Content / vibe:** Shady roadside work, suspicious cargo, criminal comedy, possible magical weirdness.
91|- **Combat / roleplay / exploration mix:** Balanced, with investigation, negotiation, and possible combat.
92|- **Character hooks:** Good for smugglers, discreet troubleshooters, bounty hunters, underworld contacts, or adventurers comfortable with gray-area work.
93|- **Player-facing complications:** The cargo may be unstable, other parties may be looking for it, and the employer is clearly not telling the whole truth.
94|- **Lines not to cross:** Keep it goofy-criminal, not grimdark-criminal.
95|
96|### Rewards Teaser
97|
98|Payment may include coin, a useful favor, access to unusual goods, or information valuable to characters with underworld or trade connections.
99|
100|### Sign-Up
101|
102|**DM:** Chase  
103|**Date / Time:** TBD  
104|**Seats:** 4 - 5 players  
105|**How to join:** Post in the Free League chat.

      "content": "1|*An Ashen Shadow Society adventure for four to five 5th-level characters*
2|
3|**Wyvern and the Wyrmhole** is optimized for five 5th-level characters. The adventure should take approximately four hours to complete.
4|
5|The characters are discreetly hired by the [[Ashen Shadow Society]] through an ad in [[The Roach Clip]] to hunt a [[Wyvern]] in the wilderness. The contract appears to be a straightforward monster hunt, but the Society has a second objective: use a [[Mind Blade]] and the wyvern’s preserved corpse to create an aberrant entity called a [[Bicephal Wyrmhole]]. The characters must survive the ritual, defeat the resulting creature, and recover its claws for study and weapon development.
6|
7|# Introduction
8|
9|## Adjusting Encounters
10|
11|The adventure assumes four to five 5th-level characters. If the party has fewer characters, limited access to magical equipment, or little experience fighting airborne monsters, reduce the number of environmental hazards and allow additional opportunities to recover. If the party is especially powerful, increase the wyvern’s hit points, add environmental complications, or introduce additional scavengers during the ritual.
12|
13|The adventure’s central challenge is not only combat. The characters must preserve the wyvern’s corpse, protect the ritual site, and prepare for an aberration that immediately attacks when it forms.
14|
15|## Key Plot Points
16|
17|**Part 1: The Contract.** The characters receive a field assignment from the Ashen Shadow Society and prepare a disposable Mind Blade for the operation.
18|
19|**Part 2: The Wyvern Hunt.** The characters choose a hunting environment, track a wyvern, survive an ambush, and pursue it to its lair.
20|
21|**Part 3: The Wyrmhole Rite.** The characters preserve the wyvern’s corpse, perform the ritual, and prepare for the creature’s transformation.
22|
23|**Conclusion: Harvest and Return.** The characters defeat the Bicephal Wyrmhole, recover its claws, and return the harvest to the Society.
24|
25|## Preparation
26|
27|Before running the adventure, prepare as follows:
28|
29|- Read the Adventure Background and review the Society’s objectives.
30|- Review the [[Wyvern]] and [[Bicephal Wyrmhole]] stat blocks.
31|- Prepare rules for tracking, flying creatures, falling damage, difficult terrain, and corpse preservation.
32|- Review the [[Mind Blade]] and the [[Graviturgic Warp-hilt]] if the party is expected to receive or craft them.
33|- Choose or prepare maps for the road, the wyvern’s lair, and the post-ritual battlefield.
34|
35|### Stat Blocks
36|
37|- [[Wyvern]]
38|- [[Bicephal Wyrmhole]]
39|- Optional wilderness creatures appropriate to the selected hunting environment
40|
41|## Key NPCs
42|
43|| Name | Role |
44||---|---|
45|| [[Zara Blackthorn]] | Senior Society officer who authorizes the assignment |
46|| [[Kezrin Malvek]] | ASSCUNT administrator and handler for monster-utilization contracts |
47|| [[Dr. Cessix Rothvell]] | Optional biomantic adviser or Society researcher |
48|| [[Velindra Ashveil]] | Optional airship pilot and extraction contact |
49|
50|## Content Warning
51|
52|Monster hunting, body horror, surgical imagery, corpse transformation, aberrations, gravity-based hazards, falling damage, and experimental biomancy.
53|
54|## Adventure Background
55|
56|The [[Ashen Shadow Society]] has learned that a rare aberrant weapon attachment can be created from the claws of a [[Bicephal Wyrmhole]]. The creature cannot be found naturally. It must be created by binding a [[Mind Blade]] to the corpse of a freshly slain wyvern while the corpse still retains its magical essence.
57|
58|The Society wants the resulting creature neutralized and harvested. The operation is deliberately dangerous because the experiment requires a living field team rather than a laboratory. A controlled environment would not reveal how the Wyrmhole behaves when exposed to hunters, hostile terrain, or a damaged ritual site.
59|
60|The Society does not require [[Dr. Cessix Rothvell]] to participate, but he is useful as an NPC. The Mind Blade is supplied by a mind flayer or obtained from an existing source, and its intended wielder must be either the mind flayer that created it or one of that mind flayer’s thralls. Any other character can carry the blade and use it as a normal sword, but cannot attune to it or access its magic. The rite can be performed by any character who can carry out the required arcane work; the ritual does not change who the blade is attuned to. Rothvell can appear as an optional adviser, rival researcher, or replacement party member, but the adventure does not depend on him.
61|
62|---
63|
64|# Part 1: The Contract
65|
66|*Estimated Duration: 30 minutes*
67|
68|The characters receive the assignment through a Society sending, or an ad in [[The Roach Clip]]. The Society presents the mission as a monster hunt and reveals the ritual objective only after the characters agree to the contract.
69|
70|## Adventure Hook
71|
72|Before the Society summons the characters to the Ashen Citadel, the assignment may first appear in [[The Roach Clip]], Stickyickistan’s underground classifieds network.
73|
74|### Roach Clip Advertisement
75|
76|> **WANTED: DISCREET MONSTER HANDLERS**
77|> 
78|> A private client seeks four to five capable adventurers for a wilderness retrieval operation.
79|> 
80|> **Dead Drop:** Retrieve the contract from the third rusted shrine-box along the [[Sootsteps]] in [[Upper South Booftown]]. Knock twice, whisper **“Gravity squeezes harder,”** to open the compartment beneath the offering tray.
81|> 
82|> **Target:** One wyvern, preferably alive long enough to become dead.
83|> 
84|> **Requirements:** Tracking experience, combat readiness, corpse preservation, and at least one person capable of performing delicate arcane work.
85|> 
86|> **Important:** Do not harvest the target before collection. Do not damage the heart. Do not ask why. More information will be provided once the dead drop is retrieved.
87|> 
88|> **Additional payment available for successful termination of a second creature.**
89|> 
90|> Bring climbing gear, rope, and a willingness to work near unstable gravity.
91|> 
92|> **Retrieve the dead drop. Do not alert the authorities.**
93|
94|The advertisement leads the characters to **the third rusted shrine-box along the Sootsteps in [[Upper South Booftown]]**, a soot-stained stairway shrine wedged between stacked tenements, rope bridges, and rooftop shortcuts. Locals leave burnt incense, copper bits, cheap liquor, and handwritten grudges there for whatever street spirit still listens.
95|
96|To open the dead drop, a character must knock twice, whisper **“Gravity squeezes harder,”** and lift the hidden compartment beneath the offering tray. Inside is a black envelope and a long sealed case containing the Mind Blade. No Society representative appears. A second document inside the envelope describes the creature the Society wants them to create and harvest.
97|
98|![[f31d3a57-beab-4c39-98b8-01495b9a0d8b.png]]
99|
100|Read or paraphrase the following:
101|
102|> The Sootsteps climb above the street in crooked layers of stairs, ladders, rope bridges, and patched balconies. Ash from [[Mount Zooka]] dusts every rail and rooftop.
103|>
104|> The third shrine-box is rusted almost shut, its little roof stained black by old incense smoke. Someone has left a cracked cup of liquor, three copper coins, and a folded note that simply reads, *“Make him pay.”*
105|>
106|> No one waits beside it. No one openly watches. But the alley is too quiet, and every dark window feels occupied.
107|>
108|> After two knocks and the whispered phrase, the offering tray clicks loose. Hidden beneath it is a black envelope sealed with a stylized ash-gray eye surrounded by hooked lines, beside a long narrow case of blackened metal.
109|>
110|> The case is cold despite the warm ash in the air. Inside rests a strange blade with a plain hilt and a faintly oily sheen along the steel. It looks almost mundane at first glance, but holding it too long makes the teeth ache and the thoughts feel crowded.
111|>
112|> When the envelope seal breaks, it releases the smell of hot metal, old smoke, and something faintly organic.
113|>
114|> Inside is a contract bearing a single designation:
115|>
116|> **OPERATION: GRAVITY SQUEEZE**
117|>
118|> A folded document lies beneath the contract. Its paper is thick, its ink is dark, and its final page has been sealed with black wax. Tucked inside is a marked map to a known wyvern nesting area in the mountains beyond the city, along with three clipped field notes on fighting wyverns.
119|>
120|> The contract lists the Society’s requirements:
121|>
122|> 1. Travel into the wilderness and hunt down a wyvern.
123|> 2. Preserve the wyvern’s corpse without harvesting it or damaging its heart.
124|> 3. Use the supplied Mind Blade in the corpse’s heart and perform the enclosed rite.
125|> 4. Defeat the creature created by the rite.
126|> 5. Harvest the creature’s claws and return them to the Ashen Citadel.
127|>
128|> The final page contains a brief warning:
129|>
130|> *The Mind Blade is a weapon created by a mind flayer. It will function as an ordinary sword for any creature that is not its intended wielder. Do not attempt to attune to it.*
131|>
132|> Beneath the objectives, a final line has been written in careful block letters:
133|>
134|> *Hunt the wyvern. Preserve the corpse. Make the Wyrmhole. Bring us its claws.*
135|
136|After the players finish reading or hearing the contract, provide the following out-of-character information:
137|
138|- The Society supplies the Mind Blade for the rite.
139|- The contract includes a marked map to a known mountain wyvern nesting area.
140|- The contract includes three practical wyvern-hunting tips:
141|  - **Watch the sky.** Wyverns are ambush predators that prefer to strike from above and may retreat if prey proves too dangerous.
142|  - **Respect the stinger.** A wyvern’s tail has longer reach than its bite and delivers a painful poison that can quickly turn a fair fight ugly.
143|  - **Do not let it carry anyone off.** Wyverns often weaken prey, seize it, and drag or fly it back to a cavernous lair to eat later.
144|- The contract comes with instructions for the Rite of Mind-Corpse Convergence.
145|- The Mind Blade was created by a mind flayer and can be carried by the party, but only its intended mind flayer or one of that mind flayer’s thralls can attune to it or use its magical properties.
146|- In any other creature’s hands, it functions as a normal sword of its kind.
147|- The rite starts by plunging the Mind Blade into the heart of a wyvern before its magical essence fades.
148|- The ritual requires continuous physical contact with the corpse or blade for 10 minutes, followed by a DC 15 Arcana check while the rite is incanted from the instructions.
149|- On a successful check, the Mind Blade is destroyed and the corpse transforms into a [[Bicephal Wyrmhole]] over 1 minute.
150|- If done correctly, the Mind Blade will be consumed by the Wyrmhole.
151|- The Society’s primary harvest target is the Wyrmhole’s claws; additional organs, residues, or magical materials are optional bonuses.
152|- The Society imposes a formal time limit of 3 days to completion before they start offering the contract to other monster hunters.
153|- If no one in the party has the Preserve spell, a spell scroll is included in the dead drop. Only one though.
154|
155|### Dead Drop Encounter
156|
157|Roll or choose one encounter when the characters arrive at the shrine-box.
158|
159||  d4 | Encounter                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
160|| --: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
161||   1 | **MOB Lookouts.** Two [[Mandem on Booftown]] lookouts are using the shrine as a watching post. They do not know about the dead drop, but they notice if the party acts suspiciously. A small bribe, good lie, or local name gets them to look away.                |
162||   2 | **CCC Collection Crew.** A pair of [[Cough City Crew]] toughs arrive to collect “shrine tax” from nearby vendors. If they see the party retrieve the case, they assume it is valuable contraband and demand a cut.                                                 |
163||   3 | **Ashfall Beggar.** An elderly local beggar warns the characters that the shrine-box “only opens for people already in trouble.” They have seen other dead drops here before and can share a rumor about the [[Ashen Shadow Society]] for coin, food, or kindness. |
164||   4 | **Watched from Above.** A hidden Society observer watches from a rooftop across the alley. They do not intervene unless the party botches the retrieval or attracts too much attention. If followed, they flee across the Sootsteps and vanish into the ash.       |
165|#### The Shrine
166|
167|The **third shrine-box** on the Sootsteps is an old neighborhood offering shrine, not an official temple. It predates most of the newer tenements around it and likely began as a small urban shrine to [The Three Sisters](app://obsidian.md/The%20Three%20Sisters), the old halfling nature goddesses of pre-colonization [Stickyickistan](app://obsidian.md/Stickyickistan). Its three rusted compartments once represented the Sisters: one for [Ashalla](app://obsidian.md/Ashalla) and prayers for family, food, and safety; one for [Darana](app://obsidian.md/Darana) and pleas for balance, fair weather, and clean dealings; and one for [Shadash](app://obsidian.md/Shadash) and the ugly prayers people only make when they have been wronged. In [Upper South Booftown](app://obsidian.md/Upper%20South%20Booftown), where ash, hunger, gang law, and bad luck all mingle together, the third box is the one people still use most.
168|
169|Locals do not call it a shrine to Shadash too loudly, especially around followers of [The Faith of the Sacred Flame](app://obsidian.md/The%20Faith%20of%20the%20Sacred%20Flame), but everyone knows what the third box is for. People leave burnt incense, copper bits, cheap liquor, ash-marked flowers, poison thorns, and folded notes naming debts, betrayals, illnesses, or enemies. Some ask Shadash to take their pain away. Others ask her to pass it along to someone who deserves it more.
170|## Development
171|
172|When the characters finish reviewing the contract and receiving the Mind Blade, the Society’s map points them toward a known mountain nesting area in [[The Outback]]. The map removes the need to find the correct region, but not the need to track the wyvern within it. The party still must follow signs of the creature, avoid wasting time, and determine whether to confront it at its lair or draw it into a safer battlefield.
173|
174|---
175|
176|# Part 2: The Wyvern Hunt
177|
178|*Estimated Duration: 90 minutes*
179|
180|The Society’s map leads the party to a known wyvern nesting area in the mountains of [[The Outback]]. This saves time by removing the “which region?” decision, but tracking still matters once the party reaches the hunting grounds. The map identifies old nests, likely feeding routes, and a few safe approaches, but the wyvern is still a living predator with a territory, habits, and a reason to move.",
      "wikilinks": [
