# Dr. Francis Norman Stein

Dr. Francis Norman Stein is a brilliant, distracted, and deeply irresponsible biomancy wizard whose experiments have reshaped parts of [[The Outback]]. His work combines arcane engineering, biological augmentation, and experimental creature design. The results are often impressive, frequently dangerous, and rarely approved by the [[Nevercough Tribunal]].

Stein is best known for creating strange chimeras, unstable constructs, and self-sustaining magical systems. He insists that most accidents are simply “unexpected data.” His body is now more arcane life-support system than flesh, sustained by a network of Magitech components, alchemical reservoirs, and magical prosthetics.

## Role in Stickyickistan

Stein operates from concealed laboratories and temporary workshops rather than a permanent public institution. His experiments have contributed to the magical contamination and unusual wildlife found in the [[Grim Forest]]. Although he has attempted to control the damage with wards, containment fields, and redirected growth patterns, his safeguards are unreliable and often create new problems.

The [[Ashen Shadow Society]], the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]], independent researchers, and wealthy industrialists have all sought Stein’s expertise at one time or another. Many of them regret the arrangement, but few deny that his inventions work.

## Appearance

Stein is a thin, elderly Human wizard whose remaining organic features are surrounded by brass fittings, glass tubes, insulated cables, and articulated Magitech braces. His voice occasionally cuts out, emits a burst of static, or is replaced by the hiss of a pressure valve.

He wears a stained laboratory coat beneath a heavy traveling cloak. His pockets contain notebooks, surgical tools, incomplete diagrams, unstable samples, and objects he has forgotten are dangerous.

## Personality

- Brilliant but easily distracted.
- Treats ethical concerns as logistical obstacles.
- Speaks in technical language even when simple words would suffice.
- Views monsters as research opportunities before recognizing them as threats.
- Genuinely cares about his creations, though he rarely understands what they need.
- Becomes defensive when anyone describes his work as irresponsible.

## Motivations

Stein wants to understand life, death, transformation, and the creation of artificial organisms. He is especially interested in preserving consciousness through biological and mechanical means.

He also wants to recover lost research, reclaim abandoned laboratories, and prove that his work can be controlled. The disappearance of his brother, [[Jonjo Starr]], is complicated by Stein’s guilt and professional curiosity. He wants Jonjo found, but he is also fascinated by what Jonjo became.

## Relationship with Jonjo Starr

Jonjo Starr was Stein’s half-brother and an amateur wizard who attempted to create a phylactery. During the ritual, Jonjo mistook a mimic for a perpetually refilling amphora. The resulting magical accident fused Jonjo, the mimic, and part of Stein’s laboratory into the **Grim Forest Terror**.

Stein considers the Grim Forest Terror both a family tragedy and a remarkable scientific development. He would prefer Jonjo recovered alive or intact enough to study, but he accepts that destroying the creature may be necessary.

## Adventure Hooks

- Stein hires adventurers to investigate a monster created by one of his failed experiments.
- He offers payment for recovering lost laboratory equipment from [[The Outback]].
- A dangerous creature escapes from one of his containment sites.
- Stein needs test subjects for a harmless experiment, though his definition of harmless is unreliable.
- He wants the party to retrieve [[Jonjo Starr]] or destroy the Grim Forest Terror.
- He offers a rare spell, magical device, or experimental component in exchange for field data.

## Mannerisms and Sayings

- Takes notes during conversations and occasionally forgets the person is still speaking.
- Adjusts a valve on his neck whenever he is excited.
- Refers to explosions as “rapid unscheduled releases of energy.”
- Calls monsters “uncooperative research partners.”
- Pauses mid-sentence to record a new hypothesis.

> “A dangerous experiment is merely an experiment that has begun collecting its own evidence.”

> “I have not lost my laboratory. It has simply become mobile, hostile, and difficult to locate.”

      "content": "1|# N.E.R.D
2|
3|**N.E.R.D**, short for **Nerds Enjoy Researching Data**, is an arcane educational institution in [[Stickyickistan]] dedicated to magical research, mathematical theory, glyphwork, history, planar studies, and experimental problem-solving.
4|
5|The institution is known for producing brilliant scholars, eccentric mages, obsessive researchers, and the occasional overconfident disaster. Its halls are filled with lecture chambers, enchanted chalkboards, sealed archives, unstable student projects, and libraries containing books that probably should not be available to first-year students.
6|
7|## Role in Stickyickistan
8|
9|N.E.R.D serves as one of [[Stickyickistan|Stickyickistan’s]] major centers of arcane education and magical research. Its professors and students are often consulted by city officials, adventuring parties, merchants, and private patrons when a problem requires brains, spells, obscure citations, or dangerous fieldwork.
10|
11|The institution maintains an uneasy relationship with practical power. It claims to pursue knowledge for its own sake, but its research is valuable to nobles, guilds, inventors, monster hunters, and political factions across the region.
12|
13|## Areas of Study
14|
15|- Glyph-based magic
16|- Arcane mathematics
17|- History and archaeology
18|- Planar studies
19|- Exoterosology
20|- Magical engineering
21|- [[Magitech]]
22|- Monster research
23|- Alchemy
24|- Linguistics and dead languages
25|- Defensive spellcraft
26|- Experimental enchantment
27|
28|## Connections
29|
30|- [[Stickyickistan]] — The institution’s home city and primary source of students, funding, and problems.
31|- [[The Loot Tavern]] — A potential partner for monster research, field studies, and practical applications of dangerous knowledge.
32|- [[Heliana]] — Her work may be cited in monster biology, harvesting, and field research courses.
33|- [[Arcannabis]] — Studied by alchemists, botanists, and experimental herbalists within the institution.
34|- [[Magitech]] — A major field of research, invention, and frequent explosions.
35|- [[Solarium Botanica]] — Possible partner or rival in botanical, alchemical, and Arcannabis-related research.
36|- [[Underdark]] — Source of field expeditions, dangerous samples, lost ruins, and things the faculty insists are “manageable risks.”
37|- [[The Silt Road]] — Officially condemned, unofficially useful for acquiring restricted texts, rare reagents, and questionable artifacts.
38|- [[Abyss]] — A subject of planar study, religious caution, and several banned dissertations.
39|
40|## Reputation
41|
42|N.E.R.D is respected, mocked, feared, and heavily footnoted. Graduates are known for being clever, curious, and alarmingly willing to test theories in real-world conditions.
43|
44|## Quest Hooks
45|
46|- **The Unpeer-Reviewed Portal:** A student thesis accidentally opens a portal to somewhere in the [[Abyss]], and the faculty needs outsiders to close it before accreditation inspectors arrive.
47|
48|- **Missing Field Researchers:** A N.E.R.D expedition into the [[Underdark]] vanished while collecting samples for a [[Magitech]] thesis. Their last sending mentioned “singing crystals” and “something grading us.”
49|
50|- **The Forbidden Citation:** A sealed archive book has started adding new footnotes in fresh blood. The professors want the party to find the original author before the bibliography becomes a summoning circle.
51|
52|- **Botanical Rivalry:** A rare plant sample from the [[Solarium Botanica]] has been stolen, mutated, or mislabeled, and now several Arcannabis researchers are accusing one another of academic sabotage.
53|
54|- **The Silt Road Syllabus:** Restricted reagents purchased through [[The Silt Road]] have gone missing from a locked laboratory. N.E.R.D wants them recovered quietly before anyone asks why the school had them.
55|
56|- **Monster Biology Practical:** A captured monster meant for a [[Heliana]]-style dissection lab escapes into the campus stacks. The faculty insists it is “mostly sedated.”
57|
58|- **Magitech Midterm Meltdown:** A student-built [[Magitech]] engine begins warping gravity in one wing of the institution. The party must stabilize it while students argue over whether this still counts for extra credit.
59|
60|- **The Plagiarist’s Curse:** Several students copied from an ancient planar text, and now each has been cursed with a different extraplanar side effect. The party must trace the curse back to its source text.
61|
62|- **Tenure Track Assassination:** A professor researching politically sensitive magic is targeted by rival scholars, hired killers, or a faction that does not want their findings published.
63|
64|- **Knowledge for Its Own Sake:** N.E.R.D hires the party to retrieve an artifact from [[The Loot Tavern]], the [[Underdark]], or a black-market auction, but neglects to mention that the artifact is still awake.",

## Role in Stickyickistan

Stein operates from concealed laboratories and temporary workshops rather than a permanent public institution. His experiments have contributed to the magical contamination and unusual wildlife found in the [[Grim Forest]]. Although he has attempted to control the damage with wards, containment fields, and redirected growth patterns, his safeguards are unreliable and often create new problems.

For several years, Stein maintained an unofficial relationship with [[N.E.R.D]], where he lectured on biomancy, magical engineering, and experimental creature design. The institution valued his original research but repeatedly censured him for bypassing ethical review, mislabeling hazardous specimens, and testing theories outside approved laboratories. Stein eventually lost his visiting appointment after a student project escaped into a restricted archive.

N.E.R.D still consults Stein when its researchers need expertise in biomancy, monster biology, or unstable Magitech. The relationship is now transactional and cautious: professors request his help through sealed correspondence, while Stein borrows equipment, cites restricted papers, and recruits students who are willing to accompany him into the field. Some faculty members want his work preserved, while others believe he should be permanently barred from every laboratory in Stickyickistan.

The [[Ashen Shadow Society]], the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]], independent researchers, and wealthy industrialists have all sought Stein’s expertise at one time or another. Many of them regret the arrangement, but few deny that his inventions work.

12|
13|A very desperate Roggan now offers **300 gp** to anyone willing to enter the quarry, find Brother Highwind, and put an end to whatever evil has taken root within. # Adventure Summary

**Dread and Breakfast** is a monster-hunt adventure set in the [[Grim Forest]], a dangerous woodland within [[The Outback]] of [[Stickyickistan]]. Travelers and caravans have begun disappearing along the Neck, a trade route connecting [[North Booftown]] with inland settlements such as [[Doobius House]]. The characters are hired to investigate the disappearances and uncover the truth behind a welcoming roadside tavern that is far more alive than it appears.

The adventure culminates in a three-wave encounter inside a tavern mimic. Characters should be prepared for a strange, dangerous fight involving smaller mimics, shrinking magic, acid, and a creature that cannot be harmed from outside.

# The Rolling Papers Advertisement

**Submitted by:** [[The Nevercough Tribunal]] and Dr. Stein  
**Tier:** Tier 1  
**Recommended Level:** 3  
**Expected Length:** One-shot, approximately 3–4 hours  
**Tone:** Forest horror, monster investigation, biomantic weirdness, dark comedy  
**Location:** [[Grim Forest]] / The Neck  

## Headline

> **TRAVELERS MISSING ALONG THE NECK: LICENSED HUNTERS REQUESTED**

## Public Notice

Caravans and travelers have disappeared along the trade route through the [[Grim Forest]]. The [[Nevercough Tribunal]] seeks capable adventurers to investigate the disappearances, protect future caravans, and remove the creature responsible.

Dr. Stein offers additional compensation for the recovery of his missing laboratory or the safe return of his half-brother, [[Jonjo Starr]].

Applicants should report to the northern road station at the edge of the Grim Forest. Ask for the biomancy researcher with the metal lungs.

# What Players Should Know

- **Content / vibe:** Forest horror, missing travelers, acid, body horror, biomantic experiments, mimics, and dark comedy.
- **Combat / roleplay / exploration mix:** Investigation and tracking followed by a dangerous three-wave combat encounter.
- **Character hooks:** Good for monster hunters, caravan guards, Free League contractors, researchers, bounty hunters, or adventurers seeking payment and unusual monster components.
- **Special notes:** The party will investigate the Grim Forest, track the creature along the Neck, and enter a tavern mimic to fight it from within. Expect little downtime between combat waves.

# Character Creation

- Create a **3rd-level** character.
- Use the character creation rules in [[Character Building]].
- Any official species, class, or background is welcome. Stickyickistan is home to species from across the multiverse.
- Use standard array or roll ability scores before the session. If you do not roll beforehand, use standard array.
- Use fixed hit points when gaining levels.
- Choose a non-evil alignment.
- Your character should have a reason to accept monster-hunting or caravan-protection work and cooperate with the rest of the party.
- Consult the DM before bringing your character to the table. The DM has final approval over character options and concepts.

## Starting Equipment

Your 3rd-level character begins with:

- Normal starting equipment and gold.
- An additional 250 gp.
- One uncommon magic item.
- One common magic item.
- One uncommon [[Arcannabis]] zip.

Potions count as your uncommon magic item. Do not use deprecated homebrew magic items labeled “Arcannabis” on D&D Beyond. Use the current Arcannabis options approved by the DM.

## Stickyickistanian Backgrounds

Choose one of the following connections or create your own:

- A member or contractor of the [[Ashen Shadow Society]], a bounty-hunting guild that collects bounties, relics, and monster components. Characters associated with the Society are generally lawful neutral and cannot be evil-aligned.
- An employee or associate of [[The Seekers of the Vein]], a mining and jeweler’s guild with interests in rare magical materials.
- A member of the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]], a lawful mercenary organization operating throughout Stickyickistan.
- A caravan guard, merchant, or traveler who regularly uses the Neck.
- A researcher or former student connected to Dr. Stein or [[N.E.R.D]].
- A resident of [[North Booftown]] or [[Doobius House]] who wants to protect the trade route.
- A monster hunter responding to the public notice in [[The Rolling Papers]].

## Setting Context

- [[Stickyickistan]] is a magical island city-state dominated by the active volcano [[Mount Zooka]].
- [[The Outback]] is a vast wilderness beyond the city containing ruins, monsters, magical anomalies, and isolated settlements.
- [[Grim Forest]] is a dangerous forest within The Outback, shaped by colonial logging, old battlefields, magical contamination, and abandoned war machines.
- The Neck is a major trade route connecting [[North Booftown]] with inland settlements such as [[Doobius House]].
- The [[Nevercough Tribunal]] wants the route kept open, while Dr. Stein wants his missing laboratory and brother recovered.
- Mimics, biomantic experiments, and escaped creatures are known dangers in the region.

## Useful Skills

Characters proficient in the following skills may find opportunities to contribute:

- Arcana
- Investigation
- Medicine
- Nature
- Perception
- Survival

Acid resistance, healing, control effects, and abilities that help with confined spaces may be especially useful.

## What Characters Know

Before play begins, characters know the following:

- Travelers and caravans have disappeared along the Neck.
- A strange roadside tavern has been seen near recent disappearances.
- Survivors report identical patrons, cold fires, and an innkeeper with an unnatural smile.
- Dr. Stein’s laboratory and half-brother, [[Jonjo Starr]], are also missing.
- The public contract offers payment for restoring safety to the route and additional compensation for finding Jonjo.
- The creature may not be vulnerable to attacks made from outside the tavern.

## Character Hooks

Your character might:

- Have answered the public notice in [[The Rolling Papers]].
- Be responsible for protecting a caravan traveling along the Neck.
- Know someone who disappeared in the Grim Forest.

- The opportunity to harvest unusual mimic components for crafting.

**DM:** TBD

**Seats:** 4–5 players  
**How to join:** Register through the [[FLS Guildhall]] or post in the Free League chat.

## Rewards

Upon returning to Ziggy Tootokes, each character receives the promised bounty for dismantling Branch Seven.

The characters also recover the following treasure during the adventure.

- 185 gp
- Three garnets worth 50 gp each
- A silver signet ring engraved with The Bloodline's symbol
- Any mundane equipment recovered from defeated enemies

## Treasure Bundles

At the conclusion of the adventure, award one Treasure Bundle to the party. Roll on the table below or choose the result that best fits your campaign.

|   |   |
|---|---|
|Options|Treasure Bundle|
|1|Portable Hole. Wrapped in waxed linen with an inventory tag reading Branch Property – Destination: Branch Three.|
|2|Alchemist's Cache. A sturdy leather case containing an Alchemy Jug, and 75 gp.|
|3|Explorer's Kit. A beautifully crafted Lantern of Revealing, a Potion of Greater Healing.|

---

## Story Award

## Friend of Ziggy

The characters have earned the trust and respect of Ziggy Tootokes, Investigator of the Tribunal Highblade Coalition.

Whenever the characters seek information regarding criminal activity, smuggling operations, or Arcannabis trafficking within Stickyickistan, Ziggy is willing to share what he knows or point them toward new leads, provided doing so does not compromise an ongoing investigation.

If Ziggy appears in a future adventure, he greets the characters as trusted associates and does his best to assist them.

---

# Experience

Characters who complete this adventure earn 1,350 XP, approximately enough to advance a 3rd-level character halfway to 4th level.

      "content": "1|# Character Advancement
2|
3|Character advancement in the [[Free League of Stickyickistan]] is designed for an open-table campaign with rotating players, rotating DMs, and shared continuity. Characters grow by completing adventures, recording rewards, and carrying their reputation forward between sessions.
4|
5|## Advancement Method
6|
7|The FLS uses **XP per adventure**.
8|
9|Each adventure has a listed XP reward. When a character completes that adventure, they earn the listed XP and record it with their session rewards. XP is awarded for completing the adventure, not for individually counting every defeated monster, trap, or encounter.
10|
11|The listed XP reward may account for:
12|
13|- Expected combat encounters
14|- Investigation and exploration
15|- Major objectives
16|- Optional objectives
17|- Monster-hunting difficulty
18|- Adventure length
19|- Risk, complications, and consequences
20|
21|Characters level up when their total XP reaches the normal D&D level thresholds.
22|
23|## Adventure XP
24|
25|Adventure briefs and DM notes should list the expected XP reward for each character.
26|
27|Example:
28|
29|> **Rewards:** 225 gp each, 600 XP each
30|
31|## Partial Completion
32|
33|If the party does not complete the adventure, the DM may award partial XP based on meaningful progress.
34|
35|| Progress | XP Award |
36||---|---:|
37|| Minor progress | 25% of the adventure XP |
38|| Major progress, but objective incomplete | 50% of the adventure XP |
39|| Main objective complete, but major complications unresolved | 75% of the adventure XP |
40|| Adventure complete | 100% of the adventure XP |
41|
42|Partial XP is optional. If the party abandons the job, fails the main objective, or causes a disaster, the DM may reduce or withhold XP as appropriate.
43|
44|## Bonus XP
45|
46|Some adventures may offer bonus XP for optional objectives, exceptional problem solving, protecting civilians, rescuing NPCs, preserving important sites, capturing instead of killing, harvesting a dangerous monster cleanly, or preventing collateral damage.
47|
48|Bonus XP may be listed in the adventure rewards when possible.
49|
50|Examples:
51|
52|- +50 XP for rescuing a trapped NPC
53|- +100 XP for preserving a sacred site
54|- +150 XP for completing a clean monster harvest
55|- +250 XP for resolving a threat without starting a faction conflict
56|
57|## Session Length
58|
59|Session length helps determine how much XP an adventure should be worth, but characters do not automatically level after a four-hour session.
60|
61|A four-hour adventure usually counts as a **standard adventure** for XP purposes. Shorter sessions may award less XP, while longer or more dangerous adventures may award more.
62|
63|For multi-session adventures, the DM should tell players how XP will be awarded. Usually, XP is awarded at the end of the adventure or after a major milestone.
64|
65|## Suggested XP by Adventure Tier
66|
67|Use these values as a starting point when assigning XP to Free League adventures.
68|
69|| Adventure Type | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Tier 4 |
70||---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
71|| Short adventure / 2–3 hours | 300 XP | 1,500 XP | 5,000 XP | 12,000 XP |
72|| Standard adventure / 3–4 hours | 600 XP | 3,000 XP | 10,000 XP | 25,000 XP |
73|| Long adventure / 4–6 hours | 900 XP | 5,000 XP | 15,000 XP | 40,000 XP |
74|| Deadly or major adventure | 1,200 XP | 7,500 XP | 25,000 XP | 60,000 XP |
75|
76|DMs may adjust these values based on difficulty, objectives, party level, and how much progress the adventure represents.
77|
78|## Tier of Play
79|
80|Characters are grouped into broad tiers of play.
81|
82|| Tier | Character Levels | XP Range | Maximum Magic Item Rarity |
83||---|---:|---:|---|
84|| Tier 1 | 1–4 | 0–6,499 XP | Uncommon |
85|| Tier 2 | 5–10 | 6,500–63,999 XP | Rare |
86|| Tier 3 | 11–16 | 64,000–354,999 XP | Very Rare |
87|| Tier 4 | 17–20 | 355,000+ XP | Legendary |
88|
89|A character should generally play in adventures appropriate to their tier. DMs may set tighter level ranges for specific adventures.
90|
91|## Recording Advancement
92|
93|At the end of each session, players should record:
94|
95|- Adventure name
96|- Date played
97|- DM
98|- Character level before and after the session
99|- Total XP before and after the session
100|- XP earned
101|- Gold earned
102|- Magic items gained
103|- Consumables gained or spent
104|- Downtime, favors, faction changes, or story awards
105|- Any lasting conditions, curses, diseases, debts, or consequences
106|
107|Rewards should be recorded before leaving the table whenever possible.
108|
109|## Gold and Treasure
110|
111|Gold, treasure, and mundane equipment are awarded as directed by the adventure.
112|
113|If treasure is found during play, the party may use it during the session. At the end of the session, remaining treasure with monetary value is converted to gold and divided as the party desires.
114|
115|For guidance, total treasure by adventure tier should usually fall within these ranges:
116|
117|| Adventure Tier | Typical Total Treasure |
118||---|---:|
119|| Tier 1 | 100–500 gp |
120|| Tier 2 | 1,000–5,000 gp |
121|| Tier 3 | 10,000–50,000 gp |
122|| Tier 4 | 50,000–100,000 gp |
123|
124|## Magic Items
125|
126|Characters may keep magic items found during an adventure if the item is specifically awarded by the adventure or approved by the DM. Finding a magic item in and adventure doesn't necessarily mean you get to keep it afterwards.
127|
128|Items that are loaned to the party, required for an objective, destroyed by the story, or marked as temporary rewards cannot be kept unless the adventure says otherwise.
129|
130|Magic items should be appropriate to the character’s tier. If an adventure randomly awards an item above the tier’s maximum rarity, reroll it or replace it with an appropriate item.
131|
132|## Consumables
133|
134|Potions, scrolls, ammunition, Arcannabis products, monster components, and other consumables should be recorded when gained or spent.
135|
136|Consumables may be used during the adventure in which they are found unless the DM says otherwise. Any remaining consumables at the end of the session belong to the characters who receive them.
137|
138|## Story Awards
139|
140|Story awards represent favors, titles, access, faction standing, special permissions, curses, debts, or ongoing consequences.
141|
142|Examples include:
143|
144|- Trusted guest status at a location
145|- Access to a restricted shop, faction, or region
146|- A favor owed by an NPC
147|- Reputation with a guild or noble house
148|- A curse, mark, debt, or enemy
149|- A License or Recipe to craft a specific item from harvested monster parts that may be illegal or exceptionally rare.
150|
151|Story awards should be written clearly so future DMs know what they mean.
152|
153|## Downtime
154|
155|Characters may use downtime between or during sessions when the DM agrees there is enough time for the activity.
156|
157|Downtime can represent training, crafting, research, carousing, recovery, spell copying, faction work, business, or other between-adventure activity.
158|
159|The DM has final say on whether downtime is available during a specific adventure.
160|
161|## Death, Disease, and Curses
162|
163|Bad things happen to adventurers.
164|
165|Diseases, curses, poisons, and other lasting effects persist until removed by magic, downtime, story resolution, or the adventure’s conclusion. Characters may seek spellcasting services in settlements or through appropriate NPCs when available.
166|
167|If a character dies, follow the table rules for resurrection, replacement characters, or post-adventure recovery.
168|
169|## Player Responsibility
170|
171|Players are responsible for keeping their own character records accurate.
172|
173|DMs should clearly state rewards at the end of a session, but players should track what their character earned, spent, lost, and suffered.
174|
175|If a record is unclear, the current DM may make a fair ruling based on the available notes.

      "content": "1|*A Tier 1 Free League of Stickyickistan adventure for four 2nd-level characters*
2|
3|# Introduction
4|
5|**The Shining Shrine** is a fey-themed monster hunt set in [[Springwood]], a sacred woodland and naturalized park in [[Stickyickistan]]. The adventure is optimized for four 2nd-level characters and is designed to take three to four hours.
6|
7|The characters are hired to protect [[Springarden]], a holy garden maintained by the [[Blossom Union]]. A fey owlbear has claimed the garden’s shrine, corrupted its calming waters, driven away pilgrims, and begun feeding on the shrine’s sacred koi. The hunt culminates in a three-wave battle against the owlbear and the fey creatures it has drawn into its lair.
8|
9|## Adventure Background
10|
11|The barrier between the Material Plane and the Plane of Fey is unusually thin around Springarden. Small fey creatures pass freely through the boundary, and the garden remains in perpetual spring. Each year, a celestial alignment weakens the barrier further during the festival known as Feyfest.
12|
13|This year, the alignment drew a **suneater owlbear** from the Plane of Fey. The owlbear is accustomed to feeding on the weak sunlight of the Feywild’s eternal sunset. The Material Plane’s midday sun is far more nourishing, but the owlbear did not account for the long hours of darkness that follow it. During the night, its hunger becomes unbearable.
14|
15|The suneater owlbear made its lair at Springarden’s holiest shrine. During the day, it feeds on sunlight. At night, it hunts the garden’s giant flying koi and lashes out at anyone who approaches. Its hunger and territorial rage have twisted Springarden’s soothing magic, causing visitors and animals to become unusually aggressive.
16|
17|The [[Blossom Union]] depends on pilgrims, visitors, and festival offerings to maintain Springarden. If the owlbear remains, the garden will lose its pilgrims and the surrounding woodland may be contaminated by its rage.
18|
19|## Adventure Hook
20|
21|The characters find the following public notice in [[The Rolling Papers]].
22|
23|> **SPRINGARDEN SEEKS LICENSED MONSTER HUNTERS**
24|>
25|> Pilgrims and travelers are advised to avoid the holy gardens of [[Springwood]] until further notice. A dangerous fey creature has occupied the Shining Shrine, injured members of the [[Blossom Union]], disturbed the sacred waters, and driven away visitors.
26|>
27|> The Blossom Union offers payment to capable adventurers who can identify the creature, protect Springarden, and remove the threat without damaging the shrine or its sacred pools.
28|>
29|> Applicants should report to [[The Loot Tavern]] and ask for **[[Threeflower]]**. He will provide the necessary travel instructions and explain how to reach Springarden.
30|
31|## Part 1: The Port Ale
32|
33|*Estimated Duration: 30 minutes*
34|
35|The characters must first obtain a bottle of Port Ale, the unusual drink required to enter [[The Loot Tavern]]. They can purchase it from a licensed tavern, an Arcannabis merchant, or another source in Stickyickistan. Each member of the party needs their own bottle.
36|
37|### Finding Port Ale
38|
39|The characters can locate a seller with a successful DC 11 Charisma (Persuasion), Intelligence (Investigation), or Wisdom (Survival) check. If they ask around in a busy drinking district, a seller approaches them before they finish searching and offers a bottle for 5 gp.
40|
41|If the characters lack the money, they can earn or bargain for the bottle by completing a small favor for the seller, such as delivering a message, retrieving a misplaced crate, or dealing with an aggressive customer. Do not turn this into a full adventure; the purpose of the scene is to establish the drink and give the characters a clear route into the Loot Tavern.
42|
43|### Entering the Loot Tavern
44|
45|Once the characters have the [[Port Ale]], they enter any ordinary tavern and drink it. Within one minute, they must step through that tavern’s door. The door becomes a passage to the exterior of the drifting [[Astral Plane]] tavern, delivering them to [[The Loot Tavern]], where **Threeflower** is waiting for them.
46|
47|Read or paraphrase:
48|
49|> The bottle’s last drop vanishes from the glass, and the world lurches sideways.
50|>
51|> For one dizzying moment, the street becomes a tunnel of golden light. Then you are standing in a crowded tavern filled with adventurers, impossible trophies, and the smell of food from places you have never visited.
52|>
53|> A nervous gnome in roughspun clothes raises a hand from a nearby table. A many-eyed squirrel peeks out from his pocket.
54|>
55|> “Oh! You made it. Good. I was worried the Port Ale instructions might have been unclear.”
56|
57|## Threeflower
58|
59|Threeflower is a timid gnome druid and a member of the Blossom Union. He acts as the party’s guide and primary contact.
60|
61|**Personality.** Nervous in new company, relaxed in nature, kind, and grateful.
62|
63|**Appearance.** Stocky, with moss-green hair and roughspun clothing decorated with naturally moulted feathers and fur. He is accompanied by a blink squirrel named Moo.
64|
65|**Desire.** To find a quiet, sunlit corner and spend his evenings smoking half-leaf.
66|
67|**Fear.** Offending people, confrontation, and forest fires.
68|
69|> “Yawns* Oh, h-h-hello. Am I in your way? No? Sorry. Moo would like to know if you have any candy.”
70|
71|Threeflower explains that the owlbear has occupied the shrine, injured several druids, and caused aggressive behavior throughout the garden. He offers the characters payment collected from pilgrims and asks them to return the shrine to a safe condition.
72|
73|After the briefing, Threeflower guides the characters from the Loot Tavern to [[Springarden]].
74|
75|## Content Warning
76|
77|Fey horror, monster hunting, radiant damage, blinding effects, aggressive mood changes, body horror, and a prolonged multi-stage combat encounter.
78|
79|# Part 2: Journey to Springarden
80|
81|*Estimated Duration: 45 minutes*
82|
83|Threeflower guides the characters from [[The Loot Tavern]] into [[Springwood]]. The journey uses three Tracking checks, and the party must achieve at least one success to reach Springarden. On a successful check, describe a strange fey encounter or an unusual feature of the forest. On a failed check, run a hostile encounter from the Springwood or forest encounter tables. The characters still progress after a failure, but they arrive at Springarden with fewer resources or alert fey creatures nearby.
84|
85|## Tracking the Road to Springarden
86|
87|Ask the players how they travel and what they look for. They may follow the road, study changing vegetation, question fey creatures, watch for signs of the owlbear, or rely on Threeflower’s knowledge of the forest. Choose an ability and skill or tool that fits their approach, then set a DC based on the method.
88|
89|Use the following guidance:
90|
91|- **DC 11:** Following the well-traveled forest road, navigating by Threeflower’s directions, or identifying the signs of perpetual spring.
92|- **DC 13:** Finding safe paths around fey crossings, recognizing dangerous plants, or locating fresh owlbear tracks.
93|- **DC 16:** Crossing an overgrown route quickly, interpreting a fey creature’s warning, or tracking the owlbear’s movements from damaged trees and scattered feathers.
94|
95|A character may use Wisdom (Survival), Wisdom (Perception), Intelligence (Nature), Intelligence (Arcana), Charisma (Animal Handling), or another suitable check supported by the party’s plan. Do not require every character to make the same check. Encourage different approaches.
96|
97|## Tracking Consequences
98|
99|On a successful check, the characters notice a useful feature of Springwood or encounter a harmless fey creature. Give them one of the clues in the Investigation Scenes section if appropriate.
100|
101|On a failed check, the party has a hostile encounter or suffers a complication. Choose or roll one:
102|
103|| d4 | Complication |
104||---:|---|
105|| 1 | A fey creature misdirects the party, adding several hours to the journey. |
106|| 2 | The party crosses a faerie ring and must find its way back to the road. |
107|| 3 | Aggressive forest creatures attack after being disturbed by the owlbear’s magic. |
108|| 4 | A sudden Feywild storm fills the road with illusions and separates the party briefly. |
109|
110|When the party completes three Tracking checks and has at least one success, Threeflower leads them to Springarden.
111|
112|## Arrival at Springarden
113|
114|
115|Read or paraphrase:
116|
117|> The forest changes as you approach Springarden. Dry leaves become green shoots, green shoots become summer foliage, and then every branch erupts into blossom. Warm mist rises from clear pools scattered among mossy islands and flowering trees.
118|>
119|> Tiny winged creatures flit between flowers, leaving trails of sparkling dust. The air smells of rain, pollen, and warm stone.
120|>
121|> Yet the garden is almost empty. Bridges stand undisturbed, offerings lie abandoned beside the paths, and several pools are clouded by feathers, scales, and half-eaten fish.
122|>
123|> A nervous gnome waits at the gate beside a blink squirrel with far too many eyes.
124|
125|## Springarden
126|
127|Springarden is a sprawling sacred garden in the heart of [[Springwood]]. It contains hot springs, clear pools, flowering islands, bridges, stepping stones, shrines, and small sanctuaries used by the Blossom Union.
128|
129|The garden’s natural magic normally calms visitors and encourages healing. The suneater owlbear’s presence has twisted that magic. Visitors may experience sudden anger, suspicion, or reckless courage, especially near the shrine.
130|
131|### General Features
132|
133|- **Ceilings, Walls, and Floors.** The garden is open to the sky. There are no walls, and the ground is a mixture of soil, stone paths, bridges, and small islands.
134|- **Light.** The light depends on the time of day but always has a pleasant golden quality reminiscent of sunset. At night, the garden is dark unless illuminated by fey creatures or the shrine.
135|- **Atmosphere.** The air is warm, the breeze is gentle, and the flowers release a calming perfume.
136|- **Sacred Pools.** The pools contain giant flying koi and are central to the garden’s religious significance.
137|
138|## Investigation Scenes
139|
140|Use two or three scenes before the characters approach the shrine. Each scene provides a clue about the owlbear or the final encounter.
141|
142|### Pyrax’s Feather
143|
144|Pyrax, a lizardfolk druid of the Blossom Union, is unconscious in the healer’s hut after confronting the owlbear. Pyrax has milky eyes, severe radiant burns, and a purple feather clutched in one hand.
145|
146|A successful DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine) check reveals that Pyrax has been blinded and suffered severe radiant damage. The hand holding the feather is unburned, proving that the feather was removed before the radiant attack.
147|
148|The feather is not damaged by radiant damage. Damage it takes repairs itself when exposed to bright sunlight.
149|
150|**Clue:** The owlbear deals radiant damage, is immune to radiant damage, and can recover in bright sunlight.
151|
152|### Feyfest Flyer
153|
154|Feyfest flyers are posted throughout Springarden. They show a five-star constellation arranged as a cross:
155|
156|- A gold star in the center.
157|- A black star to the north.
158|- A red star to the south.
159|- A white star to the west.
160|- A blue star to the east.
161|
162|Threeflower explains that the constellation weakens the boundary between the Material Plane and the Feywild.
163|
164|**Clue:** The constellation’s arrangement is needed to solve the radiant cocoon puzzle during the second wave.
165|
166|### Fey Creatures
167|
168|The closer the characters get to Springarden’s shrine, the fewer ordinary beasts they see and the more fey creatures appear. A blink squirrel, sprite, or other Tiny fey creature may refuse to respond to spells that affect beasts.
169|
170|Threeflower explains that small fey creatures cross into Springarden regularly. The suneater owlbear is also fey, not a beast, and cannot be affected by magic that specifically targets beasts.
171|
172|**Clue:** The owlbear is a fey creature and should be treated accordingly.
173|
174|## Know Thy Enemy
175|
176|Threeflower and the Blossom Union can provide the following information:
177|
178|- The owlbear deals radiant damage and can blind creatures.
179|- It is immune to radiant damage and resistant to fire damage.
180|- Bright sunlight restores the owlbear’s strength.",

## Rewards

Upon returning to Ziggy Tootokes, each character receives the promised bounty for dismantling Branch Seven. Record the adventure rewards using [[Character Advancement]].

### Adventure Rewards

- **1,350 XP per character** for completing the adventure.
- **185 gp per character** from the Coalition bounty and recovered currency.
- Three garnets worth 50 gp each, divided among the party or sold for **150 gp total**.
- A silver signet ring engraved with The Bloodline’s symbol.
- Any mundane equipment recovered from defeated enemies.

The 1,350 XP award is the completion award for the adventure and replaces individual monster XP. If the party only partially completes the adventure, the DM may award partial XP according to [[Character Advancement]]:

- Minor progress: 25% of the adventure XP.
- Major progress with the objective incomplete: 50%.
- Main objective complete with major complications unresolved: 75%.
- Adventure complete: 100%.

### Treasure Bundles

At the conclusion of the adventure, award one Treasure Bundle to the party. Roll on the table below or choose the result that best fits the campaign. Any item awarded becomes the party’s property unless the adventure states otherwise.

| Option | Treasure Bundle |
|---:|---|
| 1 | **Portable Hole.** Wrapped in waxed linen with an inventory tag reading “Branch Property, Destination: Branch Three.” |
| 2 | **Alchemist’s Cache.** A sturdy leather case containing an *alchemy jug* and 75 gp. |
| 3 | **Explorer’s Kit.** A beautifully crafted *lantern of revealing* and a *potion of greater healing*. |

The Portable Hole is recovered from the strongbox if Marek is defeated. If the party already recovered it, treat Treasure Bundle option 1 as unavailable and roll again or choose another option.

---

## Story Award

### Friend of Ziggy

The characters have earned the trust and respect of [[Ziggy Tootokes]], Investigator of the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]].

Whenever the characters seek information regarding criminal activity, smuggling operations, or Arcannabis trafficking within Stickyickistan, Ziggy is willing to share what he knows or point them toward new leads, provided doing so does not compromise an ongoing investigation.

If Ziggy appears in a future adventure, he greets the characters as trusted associates and does his best to assist them. Record this story award in accordance with [[Character Advancement]].

---

# Experience

Experience is awarded per character, not per defeated creature. Completing **Crimson Candleworks** awards **1,350 XP per character**. This is the adventure’s completion award and should be recorded using [[Character Advancement]].

If using milestone advancement, ignore the XP award and advance the characters according to the campaign’s milestone schedule.

The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. 13|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat.

20|
21|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.

23|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he believes that a red slaad killed him.

25|SLAADI, THE Terrors from LIMBO 
26|
27|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following. 
28|
29|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
30|
31|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
32|
33|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.

87|THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO 
88|
89|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 
90|
91|rest.

93|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players. 
94|
95|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.

257|Lez'LIN, THE GITHZERAI MONK 
258|
259|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
260|
261|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on the present. 
262|
263|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
264|
265|DEATH SLAADI AND YOU 
266|
267|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad. Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that can be approached in two ways: 
268|
269|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1 uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the slaad. 
270|
271|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical 
272|
273|means, such as the 9th-level spell imprisonment (PHB252-253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed. 
274|
275|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to secure the items themselves. 
276|
277|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
278|
279|SPELL SCROLL OF IMPRISONMENT 
280|
281|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to access it: 
282|
283|First, a Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire). 
284|
285|Second, a Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the shatter spell (PHB275). 
286|
287|Lastly, a 2-foot diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check, the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible. Using the Spell Scroll. A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to cast imprisonment (PHB252-253) without the required components by reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC19 saving throw (Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save, the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the spell. If the target 
288|
289|stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 
290|
291|minute, it must make a DC19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG200 for more rules on spell scrolls). 
292|
293|THE ZERTHIMON STEELBEAST 
294|
295|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
296|
297|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151), but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences, giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of imprisonment. 
298|
299|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing...

301|Zerthimon STEELBEAST 
302|
303|Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement) 
304|
305|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds. The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools. The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
306|
307|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct its actions. 
308|
309|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
310|
311|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
312|
313|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
314|
315|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi. It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles hatch. 
316|
317|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast. See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block.

If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll disintegrates.

If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes. The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand.

355|EPILOGUE 
356|
357|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control gem. 
358|
359|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
360|
361|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material Plane.

mentionables.content:
**CURSE OF SLAAD 

B 

EING A SUPPOSEDLY COMPETENT GROUP OF 

warriors and explorers, the party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened. 

Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters. 

ZARDAN, THE GITHZERAI Wizard 

Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 

Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 

Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made. 

You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the 

center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 

Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he believes that a red slaad killed him. 

SLAADI, THE Terrors from LIMBO 

If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following. 

Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 

The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 

Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 

CHAPTER 1: COMPROMISED CITADEL 

As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 

A BROTHER'S FATE 

You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party: 

SLAAD ENCOUNTER 

A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value). 

The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen. 

2 

3 

If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party. 

The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother... 

A BLUE SLAAD ENRAGED 

As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom. 

Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 

Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 

GRAVE AFTERMATH 

After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 

But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes' aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be dire. 

Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 

The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items | made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above. 

CHAPTER 2: LIMBO MONASTERY 

You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos: 

You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 

by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone 

watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of 

chaos. 

THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO 

Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 

rest. 

The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players. 

The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
